verdicts.designName: Anchor and Sample: core-omr as a model-driven sampler, not an image processor
verdicts.lens: Accuracy and reproducibility on real classroom photographs: is 99.7 percent credible, and is the COMPLETE result (criterion 12) reproducible across two shots, including which bubbles were flagged uncertain
verdicts.strongest: The sample aperture defined in page millimetres and inverse mapped through the projector, with the frame never warped. This is the one part of the design that is genuinely a reproducibility mechanism rather than a threshold guess: it deletes the interpolation stage that PLAN section 4's `warp إلى 1000x1414` inserts between the sensor and the decision, and that warp is aspect wrong for four of six papers anyway (LETTER 1.2917, HALF_LETTER 1.5540, QUARTER_LETTER 1.2870 against a 1.414 target). Graft this, plus two smaller items: the golden gate that asserts a minimum decision margin and not only a matching answers string, and locate/paper.ts refusing when measured geometry contradicts the decoded paper, which independently contains the verified one bit paper field bug in encode.ts line 85 (quick20 is A5 and its own code decodes to A4).
verdicts.fatalFlaw:
The photometric model is a single scalar pair per group, and both scalars are estimated from data that the mark, the shadow and the glare contaminate. `white_g = max(p85 of that group's own samples, 0.9 x a 24 mm box mean)` and `ink_g` = one global fiducial ink level rescaled. That is one white and one ink for an entire question row (5 bubbles over 22.4 mm) and for an entire grid column (verified in layout/sidebar.ts line 53: one bubble per symbol at gridPitchYMm, so a 10 digit id column spans 9 x 5.4 = 48.6 mm on full100). FAILURE-MODES د7 demands the opposite: bilinear between the four fiducials, corrected per row from that row's timing mark, so every bubble gets a locally predicted black and white. The design has the timing marks and uses them only for y geometry, never for photometry. Three consequences that are not tuning problems:

(1) No glare channel at all. د10 is mvp and explicit: count pixels at 0.95 of the locally predicted white inside the disc, above about 10 percent of its area the bubble is unmeasurable, it goes to uncertain and NEVER to blank, and the FRAME is refused, not the question. This design takes the plain mean of 113 lattice points, so a specular highlight silently pulls the mean up and the bubble falls out of the bottom of the absolute floor into blank. Glare is the number one cause of misreads named by three independent vendors in 4ب-1, and criterion 10 drops the build on a single wrong answer on a glare paper.

(2) No escape ring. د9 is mvp: the 1.1r to 1.4r annulus carries its own tag and is the only signature that distinguishes ink the student put in the bubble from ink that a cross out, a circled letter or a strike through dragged across it. The design samples 0.6r and nothing else, so it cannot tell the two apart, and it also gives up the one free per bubble local white reference that would have fixed problem (1) and the shadow case.

(3) Criterion 12 is unsatisfiable by construction, not by tuning. Criterion 12 enumerates the fields of the complete result that must match across shots: answers string, blank set, ambiguous set, uncertain bubble set, **glare and escape tags**, and id read status. This design's SheetReading has no glare tag and no escape tag, because it implements neither defense. Worse, the determinism gate it proposes measures `min(rel_top - 0.65)` and `min(0.45 - rel_second)`, both relative. The uncertain flag comes from the ABSOLUTE band 0.30 to 0.45. So the design's own gate is structurally blind to the exact flicker criterion 12 was written to catch.

And an internal arithmetic contradiction that indicts the band placement independently. The design states "a hard-pencil mark measures around 0.35 absolute" and states "0.30 to 0.45 is the grey band and the bubble is flagged uncertain and reported no matter what its group decides". By its own two numbers the ordinary hard pencil mark is flagged uncertain on every question. A 50 question paper from a 2H class returns 50 warnings. Criterion 14 caps warnings at 2 percent of questions on the ordinary tier, which is 1 question in 50. Either the ceiling is blown by a factor of 50 or the flag is cosmetic and there is no uncertainty mechanism at all.
verdicts.concreteFailure:
Glare to false blank, numbers throughout on the design's own formula, with AE placing paper white at 200 per 4ب-7 and fiducial ink at 40, so the denominator is max(200-40, 24) = 160.

Question 12 of standard50, five choices, student shades C with a 2B pencil. Graphite reads Y = 100. fill_C = (200-100)/160 = 0.625, a clean mark, rel 1.0, answer C.

Same paper, phone held so the ceiling tube reflects off the graphite. A highlight covers 45 percent of the 1.2 mm sampling disc at Y = 250. mean_C = 0.45 x 250 + 0.55 x 100 = 167.5, so fill_C = (200-167.5)/160 = 0.203. The four unmarked bubbles are at 0.0. The saturated points are 45 of 113, which is 8 percent of the group's 565 pooled samples, so p85 is unmoved and white_g stays 200. Stage 10 runs its first test: max fill 0.203 < FILL_FLOOR 0.30, therefore the group is **blank**. The design says in its own words that blank "is a legitimate outcome and not ambiguity", so this is reported as the student's own decision, '?' in the answers string, one mark lost, and no uncertain flag. That is a silent wrong result under glare, and it is the case د10 exists to prevent and criterion 10 drops the build for.

It is not rescued by three agreeing frames. On the tripod or scanner path the highlight is fixed across frames, which is precisely د13's objection, and agreement.ts as specified compares only answers string, identity and key version, with no pose input, so it cannot implement د13's requirement that agreement counts only between poses differing by 2 percent of page width or 3 degrees.

Second number, shadow crossing one row, same constants. A hard shadow edge crosses a 5 choice row so bubbles A and B sit at paper Y = 90 and C, D, E at 200. white_g is the pooled p85, which the lit majority sets at 200. An **untouched** bubble A then scores fill = (200-90)/160 = 0.688, which is above the 0.30 floor and above the 0.45 "it is a mark" line. If the student's real answer is a light pencil on C at fill 0.28, stage 10 computes rel_A = 1.0 > 0.65 and rel_second = 0.28/0.688 = 0.407, which is under 0.45. The engine returns a **confident answer of A**, a bubble no pencil ever touched. This is the same silent wrong grade as the open defect in STATUS.md section 7, reintroduced through the white estimator rather than through max(fill).

Third number, the estimator eating itself. A True/False question (trueFalseSymbols is exported and ChoiceQuestionSchema allows two symbols) where the student shades both in pencil at Y = 144. Every pooled sample is dark, so p85 is 144, and the floor 0.9 x a 24 mm box mean of about 190 gives 171. white_g = max(144, 171) = 171, ink_g = 40 x 171/200 = 34. fill = (171-144)/(171-34) = 0.197 for both, max fill < 0.30, so the group is reported **blank**. A double shaded question, which PLAN section 4 requires be counted and displayed at every scan, is reported as the student leaving it empty. The flip point is white_g = 171 exactly, and the estimator lands there by construction whenever a small group is fully shaded.
verdicts.salvage:
Five changes, and only the first two are structural.

1. Replace the per group scalar pair with د7's field. Build white(x, y) and ink(x, y) bilinearly from the four fiducial interiors (solid `#000000` in all three darkness themes, verified in sheet-pdf/src/theme.ts, so the black reference is trustworthy) and correct per row from that row's timing mark, which the design already locates to sub millimetre and already discards after using it for y. Then add a per bubble local white from the annulus at 1.1r to 1.4r, which is guaranteed print free by geometry (nearest neighbour edge 3.6 mm, next row 5 mm) except on the `placement: 'external'` side where د9 says to mask it. This one change kills the shadow-across-a-row wrong answer, kills the T/F false blank, and stops the white reference being a function of how many bubbles are shaded.

2. Make that same annulus carry two independent channels beside the fill ratio: an escape ink tag (د9) and a saturation count at 0.95 of the locally predicted white inside the disc (د10), with the د10 routing kept exactly as written, uncertain never blank, and refuse the FRAME not the question. Then SheetReading can actually carry the fields criterion 12 says must be compared.

3. Move the absolute bands off fixed numbers. 0.30 and 0.45 cannot both bracket the design's own stated hard pencil value of 0.35 and satisfy criterion 14's 2 percent warning ceiling. Set the floor from د8's starting point of 0.25 measured against the د7 scale, and set the uncertain band from a measured decision margin rather than a second fixed constant, so a hard pencil at 0.35 with a clean row and wide margin is a clean answer and only a hard pencil near a contaminated white is flagged.

4. Extend the determinism gate to the absolute margins, not only `rel_top - 0.65` and `0.45 - rel_second`, and compare the full result object, blank set, ambiguous set, uncertain set, glare tags, escape tags and identity, per criterion 12. Add the criterion 13 replay: every golden photograph re-read under د13's perturbation set, plus or minus 1.5 degrees, plus or minus 2 percent scale, one pixel shift, plus or minus 10 percent exposure, which is the only way criterion 13 becomes a whole set check rather than a three shot sample.

5. Give agreement.ts a pose argument so د13's rule that agreement counts only between measurably different poses is expressible in the comparator instead of being lost in a camera layer the package is proud of knowing nothing about.

None of this touches the geometry half of the design, which is the half that works.
verdicts.verdict: Strong on registration, weak exactly where this lens looks. The locate stage is the best worked out geometry in front of us and its central bet, sampling a millimetre lattice through an inverse mapped homography rather than warping the frame, is the right bet and should survive. But the confidence model bolted on top of it is thinner than the sixteen page failure catalogue it now has to answer to. It carries د8's absolute floor and third state, which is the proven open defect and is genuinely fixed here, and it carries د12's timing residual gate and د16's geometry gate. It carries none of د7's spatially varying photometry, none of د9's escape ring, and none of د10's saturation channel, and those three are the mvp defenses for the three complaints FAILURE-MODES puts before all others. The result is that the design trades one silent wrong grade for three new ones: a shaded bubble under glare reported as the student's blank, an untouched bubble under a shadow reported as a confident answer, and a double shaded True/False reported as empty. 99.7 percent is not credible under this photometry, and criterion 12 is not merely unmet but inexpressible, because the reading object has no glare tag and no escape tag to compare and the determinism gate measures only the relative margin while the uncertain flag comes from the absolute band. The salvage is real and does not touch the geometry: import د7's calibration field, harvest the escape annulus that د9 already specifies and that this design leaves unsampled, and let the same annulus supply the per bubble white, the escape tag and the glare count in one pass.

verdicts.designName: Anchor and Sample: core-omr as a model-driven sampler, not an image processor
verdicts.lens: Portability and performance: one source on Hermes/React Native and Node/CI, inside the 400 ms budget of acceptance criterion 2
verdicts.strongest: The compute budget is real, and it is the only one of the four claims here I could confirm by execution rather than argument. I reimplemented stages 2, 3, 4 and 9 faithfully (stride-7 decimation of a 4032x3024 Uint8Array to 576x432, Int32 integral, Bradley mask from that integral, RLE plus union-find components over a synthetic sheet with fiducials, 25 timing marks, 540 rings and 60k speckle points, then 540 bubbles x 113 page-millimetre lattice points with a homography divide per point and a 2x2 box read) and measured 0.29 + 0.42 + 1.11 + 2.19 + 0.52 = 4.53 ms in V8, producing 3042 runs and 2893 components. The design quotes 2.7 / 3.2 / 5.7 ms for the same stages, so its own numbers are conservative by roughly 5x to 10x. Even at a 20x Hermes interpreter penalty the heavy stages land near 91 ms, and connected components, the stage the design nervously excluded from its budget and named as its top risk, costs 2.19 ms in V8 and about 44 ms at 20x. The inverse-mapping decision is what buys this: about 1.5M reads per paper against the plan's 12M downscale plus 1.4M warp destination. Two consequences the design under-sells and should be kept whatever else is grafted. First, refusing to warp removes a resampling stage from between the sensor and the decision, which is the only structurally honest answer to rule 7. Second, it makes acceptance criterion 13 affordable: the deterministic perturbation set of defence 13 is implemented by perturbing H and re-running stage 9 alone, which I measured at 0.52 ms per perturbation, so a whole-golden-set perturbation sweep is minutes, not hours. No WASM, no native module, no fork between targets at the code level: that half of the portability claim holds.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The ingest boundary has no photometric contract, so the one number the whole architecture exists to protect does not transfer between the two targets. `GrayImage` is `{ width, height, stride, data: Uint8Array }`. There is no luma matrix, no range flag, no transfer curve, no capture-pipeline provenance. Stage 1 then defines two different sources for that struct and never joins them: on device "the Y plane of a YUV_420_888 frame is already luminance, so the camera layer passes it straight through", and in CI "a test helper decodes a fixture JPEG into the same struct". Those are not the same pixels. A camera Y plane is BT.601 luma, frequently video range 16..235 on iOS 420v, off the preview/video ISP path. A golden-set fixture is a still JPEG that went through the phone's photo pipeline (local tone mapping, unsharp masking, multi-frame noise reduction) and is then converted to grey by whatever weighting the unspecified test helper happens to use. The design's double normalisation genuinely cancels affine differences (I checked: gain, black pedestal and exposure all drop out of `(white_g - mean_b)/(white_g - ink_g)`, and video range gives fill identical to full range to three decimals), which is why this is invisible in review. What does not cancel is the luma weighting and the still-versus-preview processing, and those land on `FILL_FLOOR = 0.30`, the single constant the design added to fix proven defect (a). The design then makes the divergence mandatory in its own risk 5: "the capture protocol for the golden set must record full-resolution stills and not preview frames". So CI is corpus-of-stills, runtime is corpus-of-preview-frames, by written instruction, while the stated sole reason to reject a CV library is that "a number measured on code the phone does not run is not the number". The code is the same; the pixels are not, and accuracy is a property of both. Every constant in `constants.ts` (FILL_FLOOR 0.30, GREY_BAND_TOP 0.45, MIN_CONTRAST 40, the `max(white_g - ink_g, 24)` floor, the 0.72 fiducial fill ratio, the 40-grey-level Otsu separation) is calibrated on one pixel provenance and shipped against another, and the design's test strategy worries about "a decoder upgrade would move fill ratios by a fraction of a percent" while ignoring a pipeline change that moves them by tens. The same root cause has a second limb: `stride = max(1, floor(minSide/384))` makes the mask, the component set and the candidate filter functions of frame size, so a 2560x1440 device frame (the format FAILURE-MODES 4b-7 mandates, stride 3, 853x480) and a 4032x3024 golden-set still of the same paper (stride 7, 576x432) do not select the same fiducial candidates. Sub-pixel refinement rescues the four corners it is given; it does not rescue which blobs won the extremes contest.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Blue ballpoint, the pen FAILURE-MODES source 23 and defence 10 tell students to prefer because ink absorbs where graphite reflects. A light tick covering 40 percent of the sampled aperture: mark region R=55 G=70 B=140, paper 210, fiducial toner 28. CI helper decodes the JPEG to RGB and takes the channel mean: mark grey 88.3, aperture mean 161.3, fill = (210-161.3)/(210-28) = 0.267. That is below FILL_FLOOR 0.30, so stage 10 returns the group as BLANK, and the golden-set label (typed by a human who can see a blue tick) says the answer is there, so this shot is one counted error in 15000 and 99.7 percent still passes. The same paper under the same lamp on the teacher's phone arrives as a BT.601 Y plane: Y = 0.299R+0.587G+0.114B = 73.5, aperture mean 155.4, fill = 0.300, at the floor, so the bubble is a mark. Rec.709 luma gives 0.304. Delta 0.033 of fill across conventions, straddling the one threshold that decides answered from unanswered, and the design has no field, no normalisation step and no test that distinguishes them. Run it the other way and it is worse than a build-gate miss: the CI-calibrated floor applied to a frame whose luma convention pushes a faint mark to 0.29 returns `blank`, not `uncertain`, not `ambiguous`. The report counts it in "عدد الفراغات", the teacher reads it as a question the student left, and nothing anywhere surfaces a doubt. That is PLAN rule 6's forbidden silent negative and defence 8's "تظليل خفيف يسقط تحت العتبة فيُصفَّر سؤال أجابه الطالب", reintroduced underneath the very floor that was added to prevent it, with CI green.
verdicts.salvage: Three changes, none of which touch the sampler. (1) Make provenance part of the type, not a comment: `GrayImage` gains `{ luma: 'bt601' | 'bt709' | 'rec2020', range: 'full' | 'video', source: 'cameraPlane' | 'decodedStill' | 'synthetic' }`, ingest normalises to one canonical convention before a single fill is computed, and the `never` exhaustiveness check makes an un-declared frame unconstructable. `Frame.pixelFormat` and `Frame.orientation` are readable from VisionCamera today, so this costs the camera layer three fields and core-omr one conversion pass over the already-decimated image. (2) Tier the golden set by provenance and print accuracy and rejection per tier, which criterion 14 already demands per environment tier: a `deviceFrames/` tier of raw preview Y planes captured through the real frame processor, alongside the stills tier the QR path needs, with the build failing if any single tier drops below 98 percent. Until that tier exists, the CI number is labelled as a stills-only number in the DEVLOG, the same discipline the design already applies to the synthetic tier. (3) Fix the budget arithmetic honestly. Criterion 2 is 400 ms from sheet to result, and rule 3 plus defence 13 make a result cost at least three engine runs between measurably different poses; the design reports 150-250 ms per frame and never multiplies. Its own escape hatch makes this worse rather than better: seeding frame N+1's corner search from frame N within plus or minus 20 px is 0.78 percent of a 2560 px frame, narrower than the 2 percent pose change defence 13 requires before two frames may agree, and it makes the reading a function of frame history, which breaks the design's own stated invariant that the engine is "a pure function of (pixels, plan)" and therefore rule 7 and criterion 12. Publish the per-frame and per-result budgets separately, and drop the temporal-locality hatch or confine it to a hint that is discarded before any measurement. Three smaller items to name rather than discover: `sheet-spec` runs `new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal:true})` and `new TextEncoder()` at module scope, so if the pinned Expo SDK 57 Hermes lacks them the import throws at bundle init, not at call time; importing it also puts zod and `qrcode-generator` in the Hermes bundle, and I measured `layoutSheet` at 1.43 ms per call in V8 on all three stock templates because it unconditionally runs the QR generator at `layout/index.ts:47-48` for a `modules` field the scanner never reads, which is 11 to 29 ms on Hermes for geometry the scanner could get from a `layoutGeometry(spec)` that skips `codeMatrix`; and the frame contract handles `rowStride` but is silent on rotation, so on a device delivering sensor-oriented frames the known path has no aspect check at all (paper comes from the spec) and a 90 or 180 degree frame yields a perfectly well-conditioned homography that is only caught two stages later at timing, refusing every frame under a reason string that says fold or crease, which fails criterion 16's 90 percent reason-matches-defect audit.
verdicts.verdict: The strongest performance argument of the four, and the only one whose numbers survive being re-run: I measured its heavy stages at 4.53 ms in V8, five to ten times better than it claims for itself, so even a 20x Hermes penalty leaves headroom, and connected components (its self-declared top risk) is 2.19 ms. The no-WASM, no-native, inverse-mapping core is correct and should be built. But it wins the argument it picked and loses the one that matters. Its whole case against a CV library is that CI and phone must run one source so the accuracy number transfers; it then defines an ingest struct with no luma matrix, no range, no transfer and no capture provenance, feeds it decoded JPEG stills in CI and camera Y planes on device, and mandates that divergence in its own risk 5. Its double normalisation cancels gain, pedestal and exposure, which is genuinely good and is exactly why nobody will catch this in review, but it does not cancel the luma convention, and a 0.033 shift in fill sits astride FILL_FLOOR 0.30, the constant added to fix the project's most dangerous open defect. The failure mode is not a refusal, it is `blank` on a question the student answered, reported as a blank, with CI green. Add the provenance type, add a device-frame tier to the golden set, and multiply the frame budget by three; then this is the design to build.

verdicts.designName: Anchor and Sample: core-omr as a model-driven sampler, not an image processor
verdicts.lens: Buildability and testability starting today with no phone and no real photographs, plus maintainability: can the golden set be bootstrapped from our own PDF renderer, are files under 300 lines, can one person hold the code, and which of its tests would pass on a broken engine
verdicts.strongest: Tier 1's use of `codeMatrix()` as an exhaustive oracle for the hand-written QR reader. I verified `packages/sheet-spec/src/code/matrix.ts` wraps the third-party `qrcode-generator`, so it is a genuinely independent generator, not our own understanding reflected back. That makes the 700 riskiest lines in the package (GF(256), Berlekamp-Massey, BCH format info, mask removal, de-interleave) fully testable today with zero images, zero cameras, zero fixtures, and seeded corruption up to the level-M limit. This is the only part of any test strategy here that is both hard-gated and free on day one, and it should be grafted whatever else survives. Second strongest: defining the sample lattice in page millimetres rather than pixels, which is the correct determinism cornerstone and is the reason the design can refuse to warp.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The tiled-carrier defence does not fire, and the one gate that would catch it is explicitly disabled on the product's primary path, so an uncut 2-up page returns a confident, deterministic, fully-blank zero. Stage 4's escape hatch is conditioned on "the four picks are not mutually consistent (their pairwise fiducial sizes disagree by more than 25%, or the quad is not convex)". I ran `planPage('A5', 2)` and `layoutSheet(stockTemplate('quick20'))`: the carrier is landscape A4 (297x210), origins x=0 and x=149, gutter 1 mm. The eight fiducials on that page are all 8 mm squares, and the extremes pick (min x+y, max x-y, min x-y, max x+y) returns TL(10,10) TR(287,10) BL(10,200) BR(287,200) - a perfect convex rectangle of four identically sized squares. Both consistency tests pass, the clustering fallback never runs. Stage 8, which the design names as "the integrity check that catches ... a quad assembled from two tiled sheets", also passes, because the timing marks live on the left edge where the x error is near zero and the y span (190 mm) is exactly correct: predicted mark centre mm x=9 maps to physical 7.84 mm, inside the real 6-12 mm mark and inside the +/-2.5 mm window, with a y residual of exactly 0.00 mm against a 2.0 mm gate. Meanwhile the measured quad aspect is 190/277 = 0.686 against A5's declared 1.484, a 116 percent error that FAILURE-MODES د16 (mvp) says must be gated at +/-2 percent - but stage 6 states "On the known path the paper comes from the spec and we are done", and locate/paper.ts is scoped to "the self-describing path only". The engine's own geometry check exists and is switched off on the path the product actually uses. And tier 2 structurally cannot contain this case: tools/synthesize.ts renders one `layoutSheet(spec)` into a buffer and has no concept of a carrier page, so the synthetic 99.7 percent gate is green while this is broken.
verdicts.concreteFailure: A teacher prints quick20 2-up (the flagship template's default: `stockTemplate('quick20')` resolves to A5, and `copiesAvailable('A5')` offers 2), does not cut, and photographs the whole sheet - the exact behaviour FAILURE-MODES 4ب-7 says we must expect. Known path, so no code read. Homography maps the assumed 128 mm fiducial span onto the measured 277 mm, a 2.164x x-stretch. Question 1 bubble A sits at layout mm (30.0, 46.2); the engine samples it at physical (53.3, 46.2) - measured, not estimated - which is 4.5 mm right of bubble D's outer edge, on bare paper. Bubble B at mm 35.6 samples physical 65.4 mm, also bare paper. All 20 groups return max fill below FILL_FLOOR 0.30, so all 20 are "blank", identity is "unset", the report says 20 blanks, zero double-shaded, zero uncertain, and the score is 0/20. Every failure mode the design defends is silent here: three consecutive frames agree, three golden shots agree byte-for-byte, and the design's own margin metric reports a *wide* margin on every group because rel_top and rel_second are both far from 0.65 and 0.45. So the paper passes acceptance criteria 8, 12 and 13 and the design's determinism floor while carrying a wrong grade, and per د17 blanks are deferred not blocking, so nothing stops the 0 reaching the gradebook and `papers_graded` incrementing (د21). Cost to catch: one comparison of measured aspect 0.686 against declared 1.484, which the design already implements and chooses not to run.
verdicts.salvage: Three changes, all small. (1) Run the geometry gate on every path, not just the self-describing one: compare the measured post-correction quad aspect against the declared paper at +/-2 percent before a single bubble is sampled, and refuse with a named reason (د16 mvp, criterion 15). Add a same-size-quad multiplicity check to stage 4 - counting eight consistent squares is not a fallback trigger, it is a refusal ("uncut page, cut along the line or photograph one sheet"), and it must not be reachable only when the size or convexity test fails. (2) Derive the millimetre frame from `layout.fiducials` instead of the hardcoded `A = [[1/spanX,0,-10/spanX],...]`; the 10 mm invariant dies the day د1 lands (top/side 10 mm, bottom 18 mm), and the six-row paper table in locate/paper.ts is a derived quantity hardcoded as magic numbers in a file whose own constants.ts promises none. (3) Rebuild tier 2 on sheet-pdf rather than beside it. `docs/samples/sheet-2up.svg` and `sheet-4up.svg` already exist on disk, and sheet-pdf already carries `@myriaddreamin/typst-ts-node-compiler`; FAILURE-MODES 4ب-10 item 6 names exactly this ("علامات مركَّبة فوق أوراق يولّدها sheet-pdf وهي موجودة اليوم في docs/samples/") and says build it first. Compositing marks over the real rendered page brings the carrier page, the cut line, the in-bubble choice glyphs (`bubbleLabel` at #8c9196, 1.9 mm, dead centre of the 0.6r aperture, and #6a7176 at darkness 'dark'), the question numbers, the frames and the vertical bands into the tier that decides FILL_FLOOR - none of which the design's own rects-and-rings renderer draws, so today its floor is swept against a paper on which an empty bubble is literally white. Also: extend the margin metric to the absolute thresholds (a group at max fill 0.301 flips between '?' and a letter across shots while the design reports a wide margin, because the metric only measures 0.65 and 0.45), extend agreement.ts and the golden comparison to the uncertain/blank/ambiguous sets per criterion 12, and add a saturation channel plus specular clipping in the synthesizer, because criterion 10 drops the build on one silent glare error and neither the engine nor the synthetic model mentions glare.
verdicts.verdict: The most buildable of a hard field and the only one that put measured numbers on the table, but it is not yet safe to build. Per-file line counts are all inside the 300 cap and mostly inside the 200 target; the honest total is about 3,465 src lines plus a software rasterizer and a labelling tool, of which 700 lines are a hand-rolled QR decoder the design itself says the primary path never uses - that is the maintainability price and it is payable, because the free oracle makes it reviewable. The first milestone is well chosen and would settle the central question. What sinks it through this lens is that its test strategy validates the engine against a world it invented: a single untiled sheet with no printed glyphs, drawn from the same `layoutSheet` call the sampler reads, with illumination gradients but no saturation. Every defence the design claims for tiled pages, folds and creases routes through the timing-mark residual, and I measured that residual at 0.00 mm on the one case it names. The bootstrap answer is therefore "no, not as written" - the renderer it proposes cannot produce the failures the engine must survive, and the renderer it needs already exists in `packages/sheet-pdf` and in `docs/samples/`. Fix the gate scoping, the tiled-page refusal and the tier-2 source of truth and this becomes the design to build; ship it as written and the first teacher who does not cut the page gets a deterministic, confidently-reported zero.

verdicts.designName: Anchor and Sample: core-omr as a model-driven sampler, not an image processor
verdicts.lens: Coverage of docs/FAILURE-MODES.md: the scanner-resident defenses د7 to د16 and د20, plus acceptance criteria 10 to 19
verdicts.strongest: The page-millimetre sample lattice with inverse mapping and no warp, paired with the decision margin promoted into the CI gate. Defining the 113 sample points as physical positions on the paper (cx + i*r/10, cy + j*r/10, i²+j² <= 36) rather than as pixels is what makes د11 free rather than a retrofit: the frame is never downscaled for measurement, the code, the timing marks and the fills all come off full resolution because there is no other resolution to come off. The same choice makes د13's perturbation set cheap in principle, makes د16's uniform-scale argument correct rather than merely asserted ("طُبعت بـ96٪، التصحيح غير متأثر"), and removes an interpolation stage from the determinism argument. And the design independently invented د13's هامش القرار before FAILURE-MODES existed, then went one step further than the document by making it a build gate: "a build where two shots agree at rel_top values of 0.651 and 0.649 fails, even though the answers matched." That sentence is the single most valuable line in all four designs. It converts criterion 8 from a three-shot sample into a property. Graft the lattice and the margin gate whatever else survives. Also worth keeping: locate/paper.ts refusing when measured geometry contradicts the decoded paper, which catches the verified encode.ts one-bit paper bug from the scanner side without waiting on the sheet-spec fix. That is د16's geometry gate, carried naturally and as defence in depth.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: د10 is absent in full, and the design's only photometric gate is pointed the wrong way. Glare is the number one named cause of wrong reads at three independent vendors and criterion 10 drops the build on a single silent wrong answer under it. The design contains no saturation channel, no count of pixels at 0.95 of local white, no frame-level glare refusal, no quadrant direction, and no glare tag in the output. Worse, its fill formula is structurally incapable of carrying the information: fill = clamp((white_g - mean_b)/max(white_g - ink_g, 24), 0, 1) reduces the 113 lattice samples to a mean and then clamps, so "60 percent of this aperture is saturated and unmeasurable" and "this bubble is paper" arrive at the decision layer as the same number. د10's whole point is that the saturated region is not light, it is missing information, and a mean is the one operator that cannot represent missing. The single exposure gate the design does have refuses when the 5th to 95th percentile spread is below 40, which is a low-contrast test. Run it on the case د16 says must be refused at ingest, a bilevel copier scan: spread is 255, the frame sails through, every fill is 0 or 1, and the grey band, the entire uncertainty mechanism, reports total confidence. The gate is inverted with respect to the failure it needs to catch. Two smaller absences compound it: no escape ring (د9), so a strike-through crossing a bubble the student did not choose is indistinguishable from that student's ink; and agreement.ts requires three agreeing readings with no pose-change requirement, which is exactly the trap د13 names, so a phone resting on the desk confirms the glare-corrupted reading three times and PLAN rule 3 certifies it.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Two, both run against the design's own constants. (1) Glare, criterion 10. Take white_g = 210, ink_g = 40, a hard pencil at 55 grey (the design's own worked case: hard pencil around 0.35 fill), and a ceiling downlight putting a specular highlight at 250 over 60 percent of the 1.2 mm aperture. Mean = 0.6*250 + 0.4*55 = 172, so fill = (210-172)/170 = 0.224, below FILL_FLOOR 0.30. The group's max is under the floor, so stage 10 returns blank. The student answered; the engine returns '?'. Blank is a normal reported state, deferred not blocking under د17, so the teacher sees "student left it" and the paper loses the mark with no rejection and no warning. Three consecutive frames from a resting phone agree, so agreement.ts confirms it. That is one silent wrong answer on a glare paper, and criterion 10 says one drops the build. Push the glare to 70 percent and fill is 0.109; put an eraser ghost at 0.35 in a neighbouring bubble and rel_second = 0.109/0.35 = 0.31 <= 0.45, so the engine emits a confident answer on the bubble the student erased. (2) Timing registration, د12, silently disabled by arithmetic. Stage 8 states "34 windows of about 30x30 px is 30k reads" at full resolution. At the design's own capture assumption, a 4032x3024 frame with the page filling 85 percent of the long side, A4 is 11.54 px/mm. The timing mark is 6x3 mm = 69x35 px. A 30x30 px window is 2.6 mm square: it fits entirely inside the mark. Otsu over an all-black window has no bimodality, the dark centroid is the window centre, and the residual is identically 0.00 mm on every row of every paper. The gate "any residual above 2.0 mm refuses" never fires, and the first milestone's assertion "max timing residual after correction is under 0.5 mm" passes for the same reason. A folded or feeder-stretched paper, the case د12 exists for because the four corners solve perfectly and the error lives in the middle of the page, reports perfect geometry and grades with confidence. The honest window for a ±2.5 mm search is 11x8 mm = 127x92 px, 398k reads across 34 marks, thirteen times the stated budget, which is a real bite out of the 400 ms claim.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, none of which touches the architecture, which is why the design is salvageable rather than lost. (1) Make the aperture return a triple, not a mean: (mean, count of samples at or above 0.95 of local white, count below floor). Saturated fraction above ~10 percent marks the bubble unmeasurable, never empty, and a frame with saturated bubbles is refused with a quadrant direction, per د10. The 113-point lattice already holds the data; only the reduction is wrong. Add a second lattice ring at 1.1r to 1.4r for د9's escape signature, masked on the label side when placement is 'external' as د9 requires, and emit the escape and eraser tags as their own marks. (2) Invert the ingest gate: keep MIN_CONTRAST but add a bimodality test that refuses a two-level histogram, and add د16's dust-column check, so a bilevel scan is refused rather than graded with false confidence. (3) Rebuild timing as a component match, not a window centroid: run the existing connected-components pass inside a window sized 11x8 mm at full resolution, take the component whose bbox best matches 6x3 mm, and reject the rest, which fixes the degenerate Otsu, handles criterion 15's injected spurious marks and the pen line over a mark, and restores the residual to a real measurement. Replace the 70 percent tolerance with د12's count rule: expected N, found N-1 is a named refusal, not a silent interpolation. (4) Add a re-measure seam to the API so criterion 13 is executable on real photographs: scanSheet must be splittable into lock and measure so the perturbation set (±1.5 degrees, ±2 percent scale, one pixel, ±10 percent exposure) can be applied to the projector and the sampling re-run, rather than requiring the test harness to re-warp the photo, which resamples exactly what the design boasts of never resampling. In the same pass, widen agreement.ts to compare the whole reading per criterion 12 (blanks, ambiguous, uncertain, glare and escape tags, identity) and to require the measured pose change د13 demands, and reopen constants.ts: the grey band at 0.30 to 0.45 sits on top of the design's own hard-pencil estimate of 0.35, so every ordinary graphite mark is flagged uncertain and criterion 14's 2 percent warning ceiling is blown by a class that uses HB pencils. Finally, promote the marks string to a first-class output with د20's five-symbol alphabet plus engine_version and spec_version, or criterion 19's field-by-field record reproduction has nothing to reproduce. One more thing to fix quietly: the mm frame hardcodes -10/span for the fiducial centre offset, and د1 moves the bottom margin to 18 mm, which makes the offset asymmetric and rewrites the entire six-row paper classifier table. Those constants belong in sheet-spec and must be imported, not transcribed.
verdicts.verdict: Walking the scanner defenses. د11, carried naturally and better than the document asks: the refusal to warp means there is no reduced resolution to measure from, the code is sampled through the projector at full res, and the design derives the 6 px/mm floor independently. Best coverage of any defense here. د12, carried in intent and broken in construction: prediction-based nearest-neighbour matching is exactly what د12 demands over ordering, and the residual-as-geometry-proof is understood, but the 30x30 px window makes the residual identically zero, the 70 percent tolerance contradicts د12's count rule, and injected spurious marks (criterion 15) are unhandled because the window takes the centroid of all dark pixels rather than of a matched component. د16 geometry gate, carried naturally and independently, including the guard that catches the verified paper-index bug; د16 image gate, absent and its one histogram test inverted; write-before-card, out of scope but at least named in risk 6. د15, carried naturally in type shape (cause is the return type, exhaustiveness closes it) and weakly in taxonomy: the enum is organised by pipeline stage, not by physical cause, so 'code' conflates too-far with damaged with glare-on-code and there is no glare, bilevel or print-scale cause at all, which fails criterion 16's requirement that the emitted cause match the injected defect above 90 percent per tier. د8, carried by construction and this is the design's real achievement: the absolute floor is evaluated on a physical black-to-white scale before any relative normalisation, so the proven dust defect is fixed, not mentioned. But one branch of د8 is missing, verified by running it: fills of 0.90, 0.35, 0.35, 0.35 are all above the floor, rel_second is 0.39, and the design emits a confident answer where د8 says explicitly that a question whose every bubble clears the floor is ambiguous, not biggest-wins. That is the dirty-platen and sheen case. د7, carried awkwardly: the two-point idea is there, white from the group's own samples floored by an integral box mean, ink from the fiducial interior rescaled, but د7's per-row correction from the row's own timing mark is not read. The design opens an Otsu window on 18 mm² of solid ink 8 mm from that row's bubbles, extracts a centroid, and discards the black level, which is the one number that would make the shadow-across-one-row case a measurement instead of a guess. د14, half: four identity states are carried naturally and the positional correlation by usage rather than id string is right and verified, but there is no rule that an unreadable key version halts the paper in a multi-key exam, and د14 is explicit that this failure is worse than a bad id because 25 percent on four choices is a plausible grade nobody audits. د9, inner disc yes at 0.6r, escape ring absent entirely. د10, absent entirely. د20, partial: the four per-scan counts are there, the marks string, its eraser symbol and the provenance columns are not. On criteria 10 to 19: 11 and 17 pass by construction; 15's scale half is argued correctly and is one of the design's genuinely sharp observations; 10, 12, 13, 14 and 16 fail as written, and 12 fails in a way the design cannot see because its own gate compares only the answers string while criterion 12 exists precisely to catch a flickering uncertain set. Both proven defects are fixed by construction, not mentioned, which is the bar STATUS.md section 7 sets: the floor precedes normalisation rather than following it, and the ×0.25 downscale is demoted to a locate-only step. The second fix is one notch short of complete, because the px-per-module floor is stated as a capture requirement in prose rather than implemented as a pre-decode gate with د11's named "اقترب" cause. The pattern across all of it is a design with an excellent geometric imagination and almost no photometric one. Everything about where a bubble is, it handles beautifully; everything about what the light did to that bubble, it either omits or reduces to a mean too early. FAILURE-MODES is mostly a photometric and adversarial document, so the mismatch is real, but it is a mismatch of coverage rather than of structure: the mm lattice is the right place to count saturated samples and the right radius to grow an escape ring, and the components pass is the right tool for a timing window. Six out of ten. It would be a four if the architecture fought these additions; it does not, it just did not think of them, which is the honest position for a design written before the document existed.

verdicts.designName: Two Primitives, All Decisions in TypeScript
verdicts.lens: Accuracy and reproducibility on real classroom photographs (is 99.7% credible, and does criterion 12 hold: the same paper photographed twice giving the same COMPLETE result including the uncertain set)
verdicts.strongest: Stage 7 plus stage 8: sample at full resolution in millimetre space through H with no warp, and fit the black level from the four fiducial interiors plus every timing mark, with paper white from a per bubble ring. This is defense د7 actually implemented. It gives every bubble a locally predicted black and a locally predicted white, so f = (W - core)/(W - B) is already a number on the absolute ink scale that د8 asks for, measured off the frame at about 5 px/mm rather than off a resampled 1000x1414 canvas that only fits the A family. Deleting the warp deletes an interpolation kernel from the accuracy chain and dissolves the resize x0.25 QR problem (د11) at zero cost. The core annulus at [0, 0.78r) excluding the printed outline is right. Graft stages 7 and 8 whole.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: Layer 2 re-commits the exact defect the engine exists to prevent, moved from the question to the sheet. The design computes f, which is already an absolute ink ratio on the د7 black to white scale, then throws that absolute meaning away: s = (f - quantile(f,0.30)) / (quantile(f,0.95) - quantile(f,0.30)), and every threshold (0.55, 0.28, the 0.25 runner up margin, the 0.04 stability band) lives on s, not on f. q95 is a robust max and q30 a robust min. The proven open defect in STATUS.md section 7 is fill_i / max(fill) with no absolute floor; this is that formula with a sheet sized window and a 5 percent trim. There is no absolute ink floor anywhere in the design, and the only guard (peak - base < 0.20) is a property of the whole sheet, not of a bubble. Three consequences, all inside my lens. (1) The verdict for one bubble is a function of every other bubble on the paper, so an optical event anywhere on the page moves the decision boundary everywhere on the page. (2) The denominator depends on how many questions the student answered, which the engine cannot know. (3) د8 is not carried, and د10 (glare) is not carried at all: the word glare never appears in the design, none of its six risks is glare, and the port returns only (inCount, inSum, outsideCount), a mean, so a 60 percent specular highlight inside a shaded bubble and a genuinely empty bubble are the same number and can never be told apart at any later stage. Criterion 10 says one silent wrong answer on a glare paper drops the build, and three independent vendors name glare as the historical number one cause of misreads.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Reproducibility, two shots of one paper, standard50 on A4, normal darkness theme, W=210 and B=30 in the frame. About 300 bubbles, 54 filled (50 answers plus 4 id digits), so q95 is the 15th darkest bubble and lands inside the filled cluster at f about 0.78; q30 lands in the empty cluster at f about 0.05 (measured from theme.ts: bubbleStroke and bubbleLabel are #8c9196 at 1.9 mm inside a 4 mm bubble, so an empty internal-symbol bubble is roughly 14 percent ink coverage at 56 percent reflectance, f about 0.06). Shot A: a ceiling LED puts a specular highlight on six shaded bubbles in the top right corner, dropping their f from 0.78 to 0.45. Those six leave the top of the distribution, so q95 falls from 0.78 to about 0.72 and the span contracts from 0.73 to 0.67, multiplying every s on the sheet by 1.09. Question 31 in the far bottom left, untouched by the highlight, carries an eraser ghost at f=0.47: in shot B it is s=0.575, distance 0.025 from the 0.55 line, inside the 0.04 stability band, so the group is promoted to uncertain. In shot A the same bubble is s=0.627, distance 0.077, no promotion, so the group reports answered and clean. Same paper, same question, nothing about it changed, and the complete result differs on the uncertain set. Criterion 12 drops the build, and no code review sees it because the coupling is a global order statistic living in another file. The deterministic version of the same defect: q95 sits at 5 percent of the bubble count, which is 15 bubbles on standard50 and 27 on full100. Any student filling 15 or fewer bubbles (11 answers plus 4 id digits on standard50, 23 answers on full100) puts q95 inside the empty cluster, peak - base collapses to about 0.04, the < 0.20 guard trips, and the design's own stated behaviour is that every group reports blank. A teacher who prints the stock full100 template and gives a 20 question quiz gets a class of thirty papers all reading zero, reproducibly, on correctly printed, correctly photographed, correctly filled sheets. Between roughly 5 and 8 percent fill the guard does not trip but the span is compressed two to three times, and dozens of empty bubbles carrying wide printed letters land in the 0.28 to 0.55 band, blowing criterion 14's ceiling of 2 percent of questions warned. Independently: at the schema legal geometry radius 3.5 with all pitches 8.0 (legal today, the refine in spec.ts only requires pitch >= 2r + 1), the design's own clamp gives ringOuter = min(5.775, 3.85) = 3.85 and ringInner = min(4.375, 3.45) = 3.45, which is inside the printed outline at r = 3.5. The white reference then samples the bubble stroke, whose colour is the one thing the three darkness themes change (#b0b5ba, #8c9196, #6a7176), so the claim that print darkness cannot move the measurement is false for exactly the specs with the largest bubbles.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, all local, none touching the geometry half. (1) Delete layer 2. Put the bands on f, which is already the absolute black to white scale د8 names, and calibrate minInkRatio on the golden set starting at 0.25 as د8 says. Handle the printed internal symbol with a per symbol expected baseline computed from the layout (glyph, size and theme are all known at layout time and identical for every sheet from that template), not with a sheet wide order statistic. If a per sheet term is kept at all it must be additive and bounded, never a divisor, and never an order statistic over the same bubbles whose verdicts it decides. (2) Add a fourth integer to sampleDiscs: the count of lattice points at or above a caller supplied per disc saturation level. One field, still integer, the port still makes no decision, and it is the only way د10 can exist. It needs the local white first, so stage 7 becomes two passes over the disc lattice, which costs one extra 65k point pass, not an architecture. Then implement د10: above about 10 percent saturated area the bubble is unmeasurable, goes to uncertain and never to empty, and the frame is rejected rather than the question. (3) Make the black and white surfaces per row, anchored on each row's own timing mark, as د7 and د12 require. A bilinear b0+b1x+b2y+b3xy cannot represent a hard shadow edge crossing one row, and the 2.5 sigma robustness pass then discards precisely the shadowed timing marks, which are the one measurement that would have detected the shadow. Also drop the rule that compares a ring to the row median and falls back to the global surface: on a shadow edge cutting a row lengthwise it substitutes a smooth global white for the minority of bubbles actually in shadow, and an empty bubble at 55 percent illumination then reads f = (180-101)/150 = 0.53, a confident wrong answer in the worst direction. (4) Replace the static 0.04 stability band with د13's deterministic perturbation ensemble run inside one scan: re-solve H from quads perturbed by plus or minus 1.5 degrees, 2 percent scale and one pixel, re-sample, and flag any bubble whose verdict changes. The no-warp architecture makes this genuinely cheap, which is this design's own best argument, and it converts the uncertain flag from a property of the shot into a property of the paper, which is what criterion 12 demands. The present 0.04 is not derived: the claimed 3 percent sampling standard error is off by about twenty times for sensor noise (4 grey levels over about 285 pixels is 0.24 grey, or 0.13 percent of a 180 level span), and the real dominant term is registration jitter times the spatial gradient of the mark, which at the design's own accepted 0.10 mm RMS gives about 0.039 of s for a half covered bubble, one full band width at one sigma.
verdicts.verdict: The geometry half is the best answer to the OpenCV question in the set and should survive intact. The measurement half is nearly there. The decision half is not buildable as written and would put wrong grades in a teacher's hand. 99.7 percent is not credible under this design, and criterion 12 is not merely unproven but structurally violated. The design states its determinism claim honestly as "nothing close enough to flip is ever silently decided", which was adequate against criterion 8 (compare the total) and is not adequate against criterion 12 (compare the complete result including the flag set), because a threshold on a noisy quantity produces a noisy flag set: adding the stability band adds four noise sensitive boundaries at 0.24, 0.32, 0.51 and 0.59 where the naive rule had two. The design's own test tiers cannot find any of this. "The same input scanned twice must deep equal" is trivially true, the plus or minus 1 grey test moves s by about 0.001 and proves nothing about registration jitter, and the synthetic renderer draws student marks as uniform discs, exactly the population with no spatial gradient, so the marks that actually flip (crescents, partial arcs, eraser ghosts) are systematically absent from the corpus that gates CI at 100 percent. It will pass its own gate and fail on paper. Two further signs the design predates FAILURE-MODES.md and was never reconciled with it: risk 5 argues at length that BubbleMetricsSchema permits overlapping bubbles, but spec.ts lines 125 to 144 already carry the cross field refine and STATUS.md section 7 records that defect as fixed, which also makes the stage 0 precondition 2r < min(pitchY, gridPitchY) dead code weaker than the schema it guards; and the ring is used simultaneously as the paper white reference and as the thing د9 wants as an ink escape detector, two contradictory uses, so a cross out through a row silently depresses W for the whole row instead of raising the escape flag. Of the defenses inside my lens: د7 half carried (right anchors, wrong surface), د8 not carried, د9 mis-carried, د10 absent and structurally blocked by the port contract, د12's row registration and residual gate absent (timing marks are read only as a rotation lock, never as row anchors or as a non planarity residual), د13's perturbation ensemble absent. Score 4: two of five stages of the confidence model need replacing, but the salvage is contained to stages 8 through 11 plus one integer field on the port, and everything before stage 8 is the best work in the set.

verdicts.designName: Two Primitives, All Decisions in TypeScript
verdicts.lens: portability and performance (Hermes + Node from one source, 400 ms budget, pixels touched per paper)
verdicts.strongest: Deleting the warp. Keeping H and sampling bubbles at their millimetre positions removes 1.4M bilinear output pixels from every frame, removes a resampling stage from the accuracy chain, and dissolves contradiction 7.3 (the fixed 1000x1414 target matches only the A family and distorts LETTER, HALF_LETTER, QUARTER_LETTER) at zero cost. Tied to it: the integer-only port contract, where no float crosses the boundary except H going in. Those two together are the correct answer to "no OpenCV, one source, two runtimes" and any surviving design should graft them verbatim.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The single invariant the whole port argument rests on is contradicted by its own formula, and the contradiction lands exactly on the frame formats the repo has already made mandatory. `shift = clamp(ceil(log2(min(w,h)/160)), 0, 3)` caps reduction at 8x, so the promise "the reduced image is always about 160 px on its short side, roughly 30k to 40k pixels, so every later stage costs the same whether the sensor is 1080p or a 4K one" is false above 1280 px. Verified by running the formula: 1080x1920 gives 32,400 coarse px (the modelled case), 1440x2560 gives 57,600, 2160x3840 gives 129,600 with a 506 KB Int32 SAT and 57,600 centre-surround evaluations per frame, 4x the modelled cost and 9x the 720p case. FAILURE-MODES 4ب-7 and د11 forbid the modelled case outright ("فنختار صيغة إطار 1440p فأعلى"), because the code needs 1260 px of page extent. So the design is budgeted against the one resolution the product has banned. That is only half of it. Because a fiducial is exactly 8 mm and shift 3 divides by 8, the fiducial's size in coarse pixels is numerically equal to the frame's px/mm, and FIDUCIAL_SCALES [5,7,9,12] freezes the detector's scale ladder in that unit. Measured across the legal space: at 2160x3840 with the page filling the frame the coarse fiducial is 12.9 px on A4, 13.8 on LETTER, 18.3 on A5, 25.9 on A6, 27.6 on QUARTER_LETTER. Every one is at or past the largest probe S=12. There is no scale invariance anywhere in the design: `reduce` targets a pixel count, detection needs a millimetre density, and nothing measures the page extent before the corners are found. Both halves are one line and one constants entry, which is why this is fatal rather than a tuning note: it invalidates the timing model the "no CV library" bet was won on, and it silently breaks corner detection on the flagship stock template.
verdicts.concreteFailure: `stockTemplate('quick20')` resolves to A5 (verified by running it in this repo: A5, 148x210 mm, 24 groups, 120 bubbles, 20 timing marks). A teacher photographs it on a phone whose format is 4K (2160x3840), which is what د11's 3 px per code module floor pushes the app to select. Page fills the frame: 3840/210 = 18.29 px/mm, so the 8 mm fiducial is 146 full-res px. shift = clamp(ceil(log2(2160/160)),0,3) = clamp(4,0,3) = 3, divisor 8, so the fiducial is 18.3 coarse px against a largest probe of S=12 whose outer box is 24 coarse px. At A6 or QUARTER_LETTER (25.9 and 27.6 coarse px) the 24x24 outer box lies entirely inside the black square, so outerSum = innerSum = 0 and the score at the true corner centre is exactly ((0-0)/(4*144-144)) - (0/144) = 0. The detector returns zero response at the object it exists to find, the response surface peaks on the square's border instead, and NMS at 1.5S = 18 coarse px cannot separate four border maxima on a 26 px square. At the A5 case (18.3 px) the score does not vanish but falls to roughly 45 of a possible 220 and its maximum sits off-centre by about 8 coarse px, i.e. 64 full-res px, i.e. 3.5 mm. Stage 4 then opens a refinement window of 3 * S_full = 288 px around that off-centre point and clips at 0.9 * S_full = 86 px from the re-centred estimate, against a true square of 146 px, so the darkness centroid is clipped asymmetrically and biased toward the window centre. Exactly two iterations, no convergence loop, so the bias never washes out. Milestone 1's own gate is 0.10 mm RMS reprojection; this delivers millimetres. The user-visible outcome is `{kind:'no_sheet', reason:'no_corners'}` forever on quick20 sheets: criterion 14's 2% rejection ceiling blown to 100% for one paper size, with a reason string that does not match the defect, which is criterion 16's 90% diagnosis-match gate.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, all mechanical, none touching the architecture. (1) Make `reduce` target a millimetre density, not a pixel count. On the warm path `spec.paper` is known and the app can pass an expected page extent, so the shift becomes the one that lands the fiducial near 8 coarse px, and the clamp is removed or moved to bound the coarse image size rather than the shift. Where the extent is unknown, do a two-pass locate: fixed 160 px find, measure the recovered fiducial extent, re-search at the measured scale. (2) Derive FIDUCIAL_SCALES at call time from the expected coarse fiducial side (roughly [0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.4] times it) instead of freezing [5,7,9,12] in constants.ts, and derive SEARCH_STRIDE and the NMS radius from the same number. (3) Split `scanSheet(input, port)` into `prepare(spec | codeText) -> Bound` and `scanFrame(bound, source, port)`. As written, stage 0 calls `decodeSheetCode` then `layoutSheet` on the cold path inside an entry point the design declares stateless, so the marquee self-describing path re-runs both every frame. Measured here on V8: `layoutSheet` 1.33 to 1.44 ms, of which `codeMatrix` is 1.26 ms, a QR generator whose output the scanner never reads, plus `decodeSheetCode` at 0.13 ms including a zod safeParse. On interpreted Hermes that is roughly 35 to 60 ms per frame, a quarter of the budget rule 3's three agreeing frames leaves inside criterion 2's 400 ms. The design's own risk 4 says the type signature makes this unrepresentable; its own stage 0 does it. (4) Put row stride, pixel stride and an optional crop rect on `SourceImage`. It carries only `{widthPx, heightPx, portId, handle}`, and `reduce`'s stated contract indexes `out[j*w+i]` from a w-strided source, which is wrong for every Android YUV_420_888 frame whose Y rowStride is padded past the width; `runPortConformance` runs on "fixed synthetic buffers", tightly packed by construction, so the exactness contract the design calls "the only thing keeping two implementations agreeing" can never catch it. Also name the real per-frame host: TECH-STACK pins `react-native-vision-camera-worklets@5.2.2` plus SWM `react-native-worklets` plus AsyncRunner, so the frame loop runs in a Worklets runtime, not the main Hermes runtime, with an even thinner global scope than the one risk 6 worries about; dragging zod and qrcode-generator into it via the cold path, both constructing `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` at module scope, is risk 6 in a harsher environment than risk 6 assumes. Finally, budget allocation: `reduce` plus the SAT allocate 130 KB to 650 KB per frame, about 19 MB/s at 30 fps at 4K, so "the frame loop allocates nothing" is true only of measure/sample.ts. Give `reduce` a caller-supplied output buffer.
verdicts.verdict: Architecturally the strongest answer to the PLAN section 1 versus section 4 contradiction I have seen: no warp, a two-method integer-only port, one source for Node and the phone, decisions kept inside the tested package. It loses points where it turns those instincts into constants. The whole performance case is one sentence about 32k pixels that its own clamp makes false at every resolution the product is required to capture, and the same clamp turns the fixed scale ladder into a unit whose physical size varies sixfold across the legal paper and framing space, so quick20 on A5 at 4K returns no corners and A6 returns a mathematically zero response at the corner centre. Add a stateless entry point that re-runs a QR generator and a zod parse per frame on the self-describing path, a port contract with no row stride in a product whose only mobile input is a padded YUV plane, and an unnamed Worklets runtime that is not the Hermes the design tested against. None of these need a redesign; all of them need fixing before the first line, because every one is invisible until a teacher is holding a phone that will not lock on the twenty-question quiz the product leads with. Score 6.

verdicts.designName: Two Primitives, All Decisions in TypeScript
verdicts.lens: Buildability and testability starting today with no phone and no real photographs, plus maintainability: can the golden set be bootstrapped from our own renderer, is every file under 300 lines, and which of its tests would pass on a broken engine
verdicts.strongest: Milestone 1. Localisation only, on a fixed enumerated sweep of 45 synthetic transforms, gated on a single falsifiable number that is *derived rather than chosen*: 0.10 mm reprojection RMS over 25 probe points, justified by "a 2 mm bubble sampled at 0.78r tolerates about 0.3 mm before the fill moves 3 to 5 percent, so 0.10 leaves a factor of three," and closed with "if it lands above 0.2 mm the design is wrong and almost nothing has been built on it." That is the only first step among these proposals that can be judged right or wrong in week one with zero threshold calibration, zero golden set, and zero phone. Graft it verbatim. Second, graft the golden-set fixture format: `manifest.json` zod-validated with a SHA-256 per shot (so a silently re-encoded fixture fails loudly instead of quietly moving the accuracy number), PGM P5 gray + gzip (a 20-line reader, no dependency, Node has zlib), sharp confined to a developer machine and never to CI or to core-omr. That format does not exist in the repo today and this is the right one.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The engine's decision variable is calibrated by a sheet-wide quantile pair, and the design's own test sweep never varies the one axis that breaks it, so the 100 percent synthetic CI gate is green on a broken engine. Stage 9 layer 2 computes `s = (f - quantile(f,0.30)) / (quantile(f,0.95) - quantile(f,0.30))` over every bubble on the sheet, and every layer-3 band (0.55, 0.28, the 0.25 margin, the 0.04 stability band) is applied to `s`, not to `f`. So after building an absolute photometric scale in layers 1 and 8 (fitted black surface B from the fiducial interiors and timing marks, white surface W from the rings and rails), the design throws the absoluteness away and re-normalises against a distribution. That is structurally the same defect as `fill_i / max(fill)` that STATUS.md section 7 calls "أخطرها" and that this design is proud of fixing: it has been moved from per-question scope to per-sheet scope, where it fails on sparse sheets instead of on blank questions. د8 mandates an absolute ink floor `minInkRatio` measured on the black-to-white scale from د7; the design computes exactly that scale and then does not put a floor on it. The rest of the design has no defence, because `MIN_SPREAD 0.20` is a guard on the same corrupt denominator. And the test strategy makes this undiscoverable: the enumerated sweep is tilt, roll, three lighting profiles, three blur levels, six papers, three templates. Answered fraction is not an axis. Every synthetic sheet CI grades will be near the 19 to 25 percent fill the design assumes ("roughly 20 percent are filled, so the distribution is cleanly bimodal"), which is precisely the regime where the quantiles work.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Measured in this repo by running `layoutSheet`/`bubbleGroups`: `full100` on A4 has 540 bubbles in 104 groups (100 questions plus a 4-column id grid); `standard50` has 294 bubbles in 55 groups; `quick20` has 120 in 24. `quantile(f, 0.95)` on `full100` is the 27th-highest of 540 values, so `peak` lands inside the filled cluster only if at least 27 bubbles are inked. The id grid supplies 4. A student who answers 22 of 100 questions therefore has 26 filled bubbles, and `peak` is computed from an EMPTY bubble. Empty bubbles are not blank paper: `placement: 'internal'` is the default and sheet-pdf prints the choice letter inside at `bubbleLabel: '#8c9196'`, 1.9 mm, so the empty cluster spans roughly f = 0.08 to 0.18 depending on glyph width and darkness theme. `base = q30 ≈ 0.10`, `peak = q95 ≈ 0.18`, spread 0.08, which is below `MIN_SPREAD 0.20`, so the stage 9 failure mode fires and, in the design's own words, "every group reports blank." The paper comes back `'?'` on all 100 questions and scores 0 out of 100 with 22 visible pencil marks on it. It is not a rejection, so it does not touch criterion 14's rejection ceiling, and it is perfectly deterministic, so it passes criterion 8 and criterion 13 across all three shots and the whole perturbation set. The same arithmetic gives the cliff at 10 of 50 answered on `standard50` (needs 15 filled, id plus keyVersion supply 5) and 2 of 20 on `quick20`. This also fails acceptance criterion 11 outright ("علامة واحدة خفيفة فوق الأرضية تعود حرفها"): a constructed sheet carrying one light mark, which is the exact unit test criterion 11 specifies on composited images in core-omr with no camera, returns blank for that mark under this design. Not one test listed in tiers 1 through 3 fails on this engine.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, all cheap because the design already computes the hard parts. (1) Decide on `f`, not on `s`. `f = (W - core)/(W - B)` is already the absolute ink ratio د8 asks for, referenced to a fitted black and white surface. Put the absolute floor there (د8's `minInkRatio`, starting at 0.25, calibrated on the golden set), and demote the quantile remap to a per-sheet baseline SUBTRACTION of the printed-glyph offset that is only applied when at least 5 percent of bubbles already clear the absolute floor. When it is not applied, decide against absolute bands referenced to B and W. The sheet-wide remap is a good idea for absorbing the internal-label baseline; it must not be the only scale, and it must never be able to move the operating point of a sheet on which almost nothing is filled. (2) Make answered fraction a first-class axis of the tier-3 sweep: 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 percent of questions answered, crossed with all three stock templates, and name criterion 11 as its own test file. Without this axis the CI gate certifies nothing about the product's most common paper. (3) The ±1 grey test is a tautology and must be replaced. Adding +1 to every source pixel shifts `core`, `W` and `B` together, so `f = (W - core)/(W - B)` is unchanged by construction and the test cannot fail on any implementation. It therefore does not license the 'tolerant' conformance mode it is offered to license, because native `INTER_AREA` round-to-nearest versus JS floor is spatially uncorrelated per-pixel divergence, not a uniform shift. Replace it with a deterministic ±1 dither keyed off pixel coordinates (an xor or checkerboard pattern, no RNG). (4) Break the render-from-layout circularity. `tools/render-synthetic.ts` draws from `SheetLayout` and `scanSheet` samples from `SheetLayout`, so the entire tier-2 and tier-3 suite is blind to any disagreement between the layout and what is actually printed, and the printed artifact goes through a path the synthetic set never touches (Typst, `draw.ts`, `theme.ts`, the 2-up and 4-up carrier pages in `page.ts`). Verified: Typst 0.7.0 emits no PNG (DEVLOG 2026-08-14 checked the NAPI defs; resvg and sharp were rejected), so the design is right that it cannot rasterize its own PDF in CI, and writing a renderer is defensible. But `docs/samples/*.svg` are plain text sitting in the repo today with `width="210mm"` already corrected by `svg.ts`, so a non-circular assertion is available now: parse the emitted SVG and check that the fiducial rects, timing marks and bubble centres in the real artifact match `layoutSheet`'s millimetres. FAILURE-MODES 4ب-10 item 6 explicitly asks for the test corpus to be composited marks over sheets `sheet-pdf` generates; the design should say which half of that it is doing and why. This matters now, not later, because د1 and د3 mandate imminent geometry changes (margins 6 to 10/18 mm, timing height 3 to 4 mm) and a renderer that follows `layoutSheet` automatically will stay green straight through a change that breaks every sheet in a teacher's hands.
verdicts.verdict: The most buildable-today design of the set, and the only one whose first milestone can be graded right or wrong in week one without a photograph. The package layout is honest about line budgets (19 files, roughly 2,700 lines, none over 195, and the responsibilities are cut where a person would cut them; adding the missing defences د9, د10, د12, د15 and د16 adds files rather than bloating existing ones), the port is two methods wide so almost nothing escapes the tested package, deleting the warp is correct and dissolves contradiction 7.3 for free, and the risk section names the paper-index encoding bug, the QR pixel gap, the module-scope TextDecoder and the transitive zod/qrcode-generator dependency without flinching. It loses points because its test suite cannot detect its own worst defect: the decision variable is normalised against a sheet-wide distribution with no absolute floor, the sweep never varies the fill fraction that breaks it, and the headline ±1 grey determinism test is arithmetically incapable of failing. Fix the decision variable to sit on `f` with د8's absolute floor, add answered fraction to the sweep, and this is the spine to build on.

verdicts.designName: Two Primitives, All Decisions in TypeScript
verdicts.lens: Coverage of docs/FAILURE-MODES.md: the scanner defenses د7 to د16 plus د20, and acceptance criteria 10 to 19
verdicts.strongest: No warp, and measurement in millimetre space off the full resolution frame. The design keeps h (mm to source px) and samples bubbles at their millimetre positions instead of resampling the page to 1000x1414, which carries د11 by construction rather than by discipline: the reduce pass is only ever used to FIND the sheet, corners are refined on full resolution crops, and no measurement ever touches a downscaled or interpolated pixel. It also dissolves contradiction 7.3 for free (1414/1000 fits only the A family; LETTER at 1.2917 and HALF_LETTER at 1.5540 would be distorted), and it removes one resampling kernel from the accuracy chain. The payoff nobody else gets: د13's deterministic perturbation set and criterion 13 become nearly free. Perturbing h by +/-1.5 degrees, +/-2 percent scale and one pixel and re-sampling the SAME source pixels is a re-projection, not a re-render and not a second photograph, so criterion 13 ("re-measure every golden paper under the perturbation set, drop the build if one paper yields two acceptable grades") is testable in CI on a single stored frame with no phone and no re-photographing. Graft this whole idea, including sampling the core as an annulus [0, 0.78r) so the printed outline at r is outside the numerator (د9's inner disc, at 0.78r instead of 0.75r). Also worth keeping: the closed rejection union with a never check (the type level half of د15), the four state id reading with 'partial' and a string value so '0000' survives and an empty grid can never become 0 (د14 and rule 9, exactly right), the positional usage pairing that refuses to match on the id string because decode.ts synthesises f0/f1 while usage survives, and a first milestone that builds the synthetic mark renderer before the engine, which is the ordering FAILURE-MODES section 4ب-10 item 6 independently arrives at.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The port returns first moments only, so the intensity DISTRIBUTION inside a bubble is invisible to the engine, and two defenses that are distribution facts rather than mean facts are therefore unreachable: د10 (glare as its own channel) and د16's image gate. Stage 7 emits Int32 triples (inCount, inSum, outsideCount). No max, no histogram, no count above a threshold. د10 is not an approximation of a mean, it is a census: count pixels at 0.95 of locally expected white inside the disc, and above about 10 percent of its area the bubble is not light, it is UNMEASURABLE, goes to uncertain, never to blank, and the FRAME is rejected with a quadrant and a direction to move. The design has no glare channel, no saturation count, no glare rejection reason (its enum is too_far, no_corners, quad_rejected, low_contrast, paper_ambiguous, lock_failed, off_frame, spec_mismatch), and no glare tag on the reading, which also makes criterion 12 unstatable since criterion 12 requires the compared result to include the glare and escape tags. Specular reflection off graphite is the number one named cause of wrong reads in three independent vendor documents (sources 1, 2, 3) and the failure direction here is the worst one: a saturated blob raises the core mean, f falls, and a shaded bubble reads EMPTY with a huge decision margin. Every determinism mechanism in the design then confirms the error instead of catching it. The stability band sees a margin of 0.15 and stays quiet, the +/-1 grey test does not move a saturated pixel, three frames from a hand or a stand agree, and the perturbation set re-samples the same saturated pixels. The design converts the competitor's flickering wrong grade into a stable, reproducible, silent wrong grade, which is worse for the teacher because there is no signal at all. Criterion 10 is explicit: on the glare layer the acceptable outputs are a correct read or a rejection, and one wrong answer drops the build. Fixing it is not a constant change, it is a change to the two method port contract the whole design is named after, and it has an ordering problem on top: the locally expected white comes from the ring means and the levels fit in stage 8, which run AFTER the stage 7 sampling call, so a locally referenced saturation census needs either a fixed absolute threshold passed in at sample time or a second full sampling pass (another 65k lattice points) after the levels are known. The same sum-only limitation blocks د16's bilevel and JBIG2 gate: in a two level image every bubble reads f of exactly 0 or 1, the quantile remap produces a textbook bimodal distribution, MIN_SPREAD passes, every margin is maximal, and the engine reports total confidence on an image whose grey range was destroyed, which is the exact sentence د16 uses ("فتبلّغ آلية الشك عندنا عن ثقة تامة").
verdicts.concreteFailure:
Glare, with numbers on the design's own constants. Paper white W = 200, black surface B = 20, a properly shaded bubble core = 25. A specular highlight covering 60 percent of the inner disc (the disc is 2 * 0.78 * 2mm = 3.1mm across, and a point source highlight on graphite is a few millimetres) gives core = 0.6*255 + 0.4*25 = 163. f = (200 - 163) / (200 - 20) = 0.206. With BASE_Q 0.30 at about 0.10 and PEAK_Q 0.95 at about 0.95, s = (0.206 - 0.10)/0.85 = 0.125, which is below T_EMPTY 0.28 by 0.155, nearly four times STABILITY 0.04, so the group is decided, not promoted to uncertain. The shaded answer is reported blank, or, if a neighbouring option carries an eraser ghost above 0.55, reported as the wrong letter with full confidence. At 40 percent coverage it lands at s = 0.42 and is merely uncertain, so the whole glare failure mode sits on a coverage knife edge between "flagged" and "silently wrong" that nothing in the design measures.

Second, and this is the first proven defect returning in new clothes. Measured in this repo: standard50 has 294 bubbles (250 question plus 44 grid) and 25 timing marks. A fully answered sheet has 50 + 4 + 1 = 55 filled, about 19 percent, which is the design's stated premise. PEAK_Q 0.95 over 294 bubbles is the 15th darkest bubble. A student who answers 9 of 50 questions has 9 + 5 = 14 filled, so the 15th darkest is an EMPTY bubble carrying its printed letter, peak becomes about 0.18 against base about 0.10, peak - base = 0.08 which is under MIN_SPREAD 0.20, and stage 9's stated failure path fires: "every group reports blank". The paper is graded 0 out of 50 and reported as fifty blanks, which is a decided state (د8: blank is the student's decision), not a rejection. At 10 to 12 answered questions the sheet sits exactly on the rank 15 boundary, so under criterion 13's own perturbation set (+/-1.5 degrees, +/-2 percent scale, one pixel) the rank ordering near 15 flips, peak jumps between about 0.85 and about 0.18, the divisor (peak - base) changes by a factor of nine, and every s on the sheet rescales at once. One pose grades 10 out of 50, another grades 0 out of 50. That is two acceptable grades for one paper, which drops the build under criterion 13 and criterion 8, and it is produced entirely by the design's own published constants on a template that exists in the repo today.
