Third, cheap and certain: on a `placement: 'external'` sheet the white reference is contaminated by print. grid.ts puts the label slot at [cellLeft, cellLeft + externalLabelMm 3.2] with the bubble centre at cellLeft + 3.2 + r, so printed glyph ink reaches to exactly r (2.0mm) from the bubble centre, entirely inside the ring [1.25r, 1.65r] = [2.5, 3.3]mm. د9 names this constraint and masks the ring on the label side; this design does not, and it is worse here than for د9 because the ring is load bearing as WHITE, not as an ink detector. Every bubble in the row is depressed identically, so the "within tolerance of the row median ring" fallback never fires, W drops from 200 to about 176, and a genuine 35 percent mark measures f = (176 - 137)/156 = 0.25 instead of 0.35, pushing light shading toward blank across the whole sheet in one direction. Also verified: the schema refine at spec.ts already forces pitch >= 2r + 1mm (the overlap defect in the design's risk 5 is fixed upstream), and full100 runs gridPitchYMm 5.4 at r = 2, so ringOuter clamps to min(3.3, 2.55) = 2.55 and ringInner to 2.15, putting the "guaranteed paper" annulus 0.15mm from a bubbleStroke that is 0.2 to 0.32mm wide depending on the darkness theme. The design's claim that the three print themes cannot move the measurement is true of the core and false of the ring.
verdicts.salvage: Five changes, the first two structural. (1) Widen sampleDiscs by one channel: return a saturation census alongside the sum, either countAtOrAbove(absoluteThreshold) with the threshold passed in at call time, or a fixed 8 bin histogram of the disc's samples. That single number carries د10 (glare) and د16's bilevel gate at once, since both are distribution facts; add `glare` to the rejection enum with the quadrant that holds the saturation and the direction to move, add a glare tag and an escape tag to the reading so criterion 12's comparison set can be stated, and accept either a fixed absolute saturation threshold in stage 7 or a second cheap disc pass after the levels fit so the 0.95-of-local-white test in د10 is literally what runs. Rule: a saturated bubble goes to uncertain and never to blank, and the frame is rejected, not the question. (2) Put the absolute floor back where د8 put it. The design already computes f on the د7 black to white scale, which is an absolute ink ratio, and then throws that property away by thresholding only on the sheet-relative s. Threshold f against minInkRatio (د8 starts at 0.25 and earns it on the golden set) BEFORE any quantile remap, keep the remap as a refinement that can only make a group more conservative, and make peak independent of how many questions the student answered. Then criterion 11 (a clean row returns '?' in 100 percent of cases, a speck at 3x, 5x and 10x the noise floor still returns '?', one light mark above the floor returns its letter) becomes a property of the per-bubble arithmetic instead of a property of student behaviour. (3) Measure the timing marks instead of verifying them. Sample a lattice down the left rail, take darkness weighted centroids, emit the count (so "expected 34, found 33" is a named rejection rather than a silent renumbering), the per-mark residual against prediction with د12's 0.5mm RMS gate, and a per-row y correction so a bowed or fed-stretched page is registered rather than rejected. This also splits `lock_failed`, which today conflates a wrong template, a rotated sheet, a bowed page, a covered mark and a starved print into one reason with no physical cause, violating د15 in the same breath the design satisfies its type-level half; and criterion 15's occlusion test (hide k of N marks, inject k false ones, row numbering stable to 20 percent) is unpassable until marks are detected rather than probed. (4) Separate the escape ring from the white reference. د9's escape annulus [1.1r, 1.4r] exists to say "the ink left the bubble", which is the signature of a circled letter, a cross out and a strikethrough, and it needs its own tag; the white reference belongs on the rails and on masked sectors, with the label side masked whenever placement is 'external'. Without this, a circled answer reads blank in silence, and د20's marks alphabet loses its eraser symbol, so criterion 19 (the paper reproduces its own record field by field including the marks string) cannot be met. (5) Add rejection accounting to the test tiers. Criterion 14 requires accuracy and rejection rate printed together, an ordinary layer at no more than 2 percent papers rejected and 2 percent questions warned, an adversarial layer where rejection IS success, and per-environment-layer accuracy with the build dropping if one layer falls under 98 percent even when the total passes. The design's CI gate measures accuracy only, and it adds whole-frame rejections (paper_ambiguous, lock_failed, low_contrast, off_frame) plus a group promotion band with no budget attached to any of them.
verdicts.verdict: Walking the defenses. د7 photometric calibration from the sheet: carried, awkwardly. The machinery is right and is the design's second best idea (black from the four fiducial interiors plus every timing mark, white from the per-bubble rings and the white rails, both pure #000000 in all three themes), but the spatial model is inconsistent: W is estimated locally per bubble while B is a single global bilinear b0 + b1x + b2y + b3xy. د7 asks for a per-row correction from that row's own timing mark, and the named failure it exists for is a hard shadow cutting ONE row, which a bilinear surface cannot represent. Concretely, with a shadow over the bottom third, the fit lands B at about 16 where the true local black is 8 in shadow and 20 in light, so the shadowed third reads about 10 percent hotter in f, uniformly, and the sheet-wide quantile remap does not remove a regional bias. That produces correlated errors concentrated in one part of the page, which the failure table calls the hardest signature to notice. د8 absolute floor and blank as a third state: half carried, and this is where proven defect (a) survives. Blank is a genuine named state, which is real progress over the sketch, but there is no absolute ink floor anywhere: the operative thresholds T_FILLED 0.55 and T_EMPTY 0.28 are applied to s, a sheet-relative remap between quantile 0.30 and quantile 0.95, so the denominator is again a statistic of the marks rather than of the ink, just computed over 294 bubbles instead of 5. The design had the absolute quantity in hand and declined to threshold it. د9 inner disc and escape ring: half. Inner disc at 0.78r is exactly right; the escape ring is not implemented as an escape ring at all, it is repurposed as the white reference, which is the inverse reading of the same annulus, and the row-median fallback actively suppresses the signal د9 wants raised. No masking for external placement, which the geometry in grid.ts shows is required. د10 glare: structurally cannot, see the fatal flaw. د11 measuring off the full resolution frame: carried naturally and better than the doc asks, the design's standout. Two shortfalls: MIN_SCALE_PX_PER_MM 3.2 is half of the 6 px/mm that د11 derives from 3 px per 0.5mm code module (a 1260 px page span), and there is no "come closer" rejection, only a too_far gate on frames under 320 px. د12 timing marks: not carried. The marks are probed at predicted positions for a dark fraction, never measured, so there is no residual, no count, no nearest-neighbour matching and no per-row registration, and all three of د12's uses are missing from a design that otherwise samples everything else beautifully. د13 decision margin and the deterministic perturbation set: carried, and the no-warp choice makes the perturbation set almost free, which is the best structural fit in the whole document. But the design substitutes a +/-1 grey test for the +/-1.5 degree, +/-2 percent, one pixel set it never names, and STABILITY 0.04 is called derived when the derivation is loose: the inner disc at 0.78r on a 2mm bubble at 5 px/mm holds about 191 independent pixels, not the 285 claimed, and at the design's own accepted floor of 3.2 px/mm it is about 78, so the constant band covers well under one sigma exactly where resolution is worst. د14 grids never resolved and partial as a fourth state: carried naturally and precisely, including the refusal to invent a zero and the positional usage pairing. The half that is missing is the key version, which د14 says is stricter than the id rule because its failure is silent (a wrong key yields a plausible 25 percent); the design names only usage 'studentId' and moves key comparison out of the package entirely, so nothing in any layer is contracted to stop the paper. د15 closed enum with a physical cause: half. The type-level discipline is exemplary and criterion 16's never check is satisfied, but the enum is missing glare, bilevel, geometry mismatch, wrong exam and print scale, and lock_failed alone conflates four physically distinct causes, which is exactly the "sharpness slider" non-diagnosis the doc mocks; criterion 16's second half (emitted cause matches injected defect above 90 percent per layer) is unreachable with the causes on offer. د16 acceptance gates: the geometry gate is only on the cold path, because paper-guess.ts runs when no spec is supplied and the design's own risk section says the warm path is essentially every scan, so criterion 15's demand that a mis-measured sheet be rejected with geometry NAMED has no implementation; the byte-identical-score-across-print-scales half is carried naturally by the four corner fit. Write before card is correctly out of package. د20 the marks string: derivable for four of five symbols; the eraser trace has no source because the escape ring was spent on white. Criteria: 10 fails, 11 passes on ordinary sheets and fails on sparse ones, 12 cannot be stated (no glare or escape tags), 13 has the right mechanism but the sheet-wide quantile couples every bubble to every other one and threatens it, 14 has no accounting at all, 15 fails on occlusion and on naming, 16 passes at the type level and fails at the diagnosis level, 17 is natural (no image bytes are written; the name crop stays in memory), 18 is out of package, 19 is nearly carried. On the two proven defects: (b), full resolution measurement, is fixed by construction and then some, since the design never warps or downscales in the measurement path at all. (a), the threshold with no absolute floor, is NOT fixed by construction. It is relocated from max(fill) per question to quantile 0.95 per sheet, which is the same relative-denominator sin with a larger sample and one new failure the original did not have, namely that a sparsely answered paper drives its own denominator into the empty cluster. STATUS.md section 7 says this one must be built correct from the first line, and as written it is not. This is a strong engine wearing the wrong armour: it should be rebuilt around an absolute per-bubble ink ratio, a saturation census, and measured timing marks, keeping the no-warp core, the integer port and the four-state id intact.

verdicts.designName: Paper-Space Sampling: core-omr without a warp and without OpenCV
verdicts.lens: Accuracy and reproducibility on real classroom photographs: is 99.7 percent credible, and is the COMPLETE result (criterion 12) identical across two shots of one paper
verdicts.strongest: The continuity discipline and the margin distribution promoted to a build gate. Fixing the sample set in millimetres and inverse-mapping it through H means both photographs integrate the SAME physical graphite, so pose dependence collapses to homography residual; banning every discontinuous operator upstream (weighted centroid instead of contour moments, fixed-size lattice means, nearest-rank percentiles, no RANSAC, no Otsu, no data-dependent iteration) makes the disagreement probability equal to the straddle probability of one scalar; and then p01 of decided-bubble margin >= 0.06 with p01 of groupGap >= 0.15 turns that into a number CI can fail on. That is the only place in the four-design set where determinism is an engineering argument with a measurement attached instead of a hope, and it is exactly د13's «هامش قرار يُخرَج مع كل فقاعة». Keep it whole, including the tier-0 fingerprint gate on day one.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The photometric half is anchored on an extreme order statistic and has no channel for missing information. (1) M = nearest-rank p99 makes every bubble's fate a function of the two or three darkest bubbles on that sheet (verified by running layoutSheet: quick20 = 120 bubbles so M is the 2nd darkest, standard50 = 294 so the 3rd, full100 = 540 so the 6th). One local artifact rescales all 294 decisions. (2) There is no absolute ink floor anywhere in constants.ts, so د8's `minInkRatio` is not carried: the proven defect 3a is not eliminated, only moved from per-question to per-page, where it fires whenever the darkest three things on the paper are not marks. (3) Glare, the number one field-reported cause of wrong reads and the subject of د10, is not modelled at all. Ink is a scalar, and a specular highlight drives it DOWN: with paper 210, toner 40, graphite 120, once saturation covers about 45 percent of the 2.48 mm core the filled bubble scores below T_LO and reads confidently BLANK with margin ~0.09. Criterion 10 fails the build on one occurrence, and because a phone under a fixed lamp reproduces the highlight, rule 3's three frames and this design's own fingerprint gate both bless the wrong answer. The only contrast gate (white - black < 28) never fires, because glare is inside the core and the lobes stay paper. (4) black(x,y) is bilinear from the four corners only, so د7's stated requirement («مصحَّحة لكل صف من علامة توقيته») is dropped even though stage 6 already centroids every timing mark at full resolution: a hard shadow edge across one row at 50 percent illumination scales white but not the interpolated black, inflating that row's ink by 31 percent, up to +0.2 in score, which is 80 percent of the whole uncertain band. (5) p70 over the lobes consumes د9's escape ring as noise instead of reporting it, so circling, crossing out and spill have no signature. (6) readFingerprint canonicalises question and field verdicts only; criterion 12 literally enumerates six things to compare, including the per-bubble uncertain set and the glare and escape tags, which do not exist in this design. Two shots can agree on every verdict, differ on which bubble was uncertain, and pass.
verdicts.concreteFailure: standard50, A4, verified by running the repo's layoutSheet and bubbleGroups: 55 groups, 294 bubbles, so nearest-rank p99 = ascending rank 292 = the THIRD darkest bubble on the page. The 4-bubble studentId grid is the part of the sheet a student fills first and hardest. Take an ordinary paper: four ID bubbles plus one re-darkened answer at ink 0.55, the other 49 answers at a normal 0.29, blanks at B = 0.03. M = 0.55, so every ordinary answer scores (0.29 - 0.03) / (0.55 - 0.03) = 0.50, inside the 0.30 to 0.55 band. The engine returns 49 of 50 questions ambiguous on a cleanly answered paper. No gate fires: M - B = 0.52, far above SHEET_UNMARKED_RANGE = 0.12, and there is no rejection reason to show, so the teacher gets 49 manual decisions with no explanation. Margin is 0.05, under the design's own p01 floor of 0.06, so ordinary shot-to-shot noise flips individual bubbles between marked and uncertain: the answers string, the uncertain set and the ambiguous set all differ between two photographs of that one paper. Criteria 8, 12 and 14 fail together on one ordinary sheet. On quick20 it is worse, M is the 2nd darkest of 120, so two carefully filled ID digits are enough. Run the same estimator the other way and the proven defect returns: a nearly blank paper with two genuine marks and a graphite hand-drag across three bubbles at ink 0.30 makes the drag the top three, M = 0.30, each smudged bubble scores 1.00 and clears GROUP_GAP_MIN = 0.30 against its blank neighbours, so three untouched questions come back as confident answers with wide margins. That is the silent wrong grade in STATUS section 7, still alive.
verdicts.salvage: Stages 1 to 7 can be written today. Stages 8 to 10 must be rebuilt against د7 to د10 first, and none of the fixes touch the architecture. (a) Replace M = p99 with a robust centre of the mark cluster: the median of per-group top-1 ink over groups whose top-1 clears an absolute floor, clamped into a plausible band relative to the black anchor. Anchoring on the centre of the marks, not on their extreme, removes the global coupling; report the mark-cluster dispersion so a bimodal-pressure paper is a named state, not 49 ambiguities. (b) Add MIN_INK_ABS to constants.ts implementing د8's `minInkRatio` on the same paper-to-toner scale, and compute no relative score until it is crossed, so a page whose darkest three items are dust or a smudge is blank, not answered. (c) Add the saturation channel د10 specifies: count core samples at or above 0.95 of local white; above about 10 percent of core area the bubble is unmeasurable, which routes to uncertain and never to blank, and reject the FRAME with the quadrant so the instruction is actionable. (d) Take black per row from that row's timing-mark interior luma, which stage 6 already locates at full resolution, and interpolate only along the row; keep the corner bilinear as the fallback where no mark exists (header band, sidebar). (e) Split the ring into two statistics: p70 for local white AND a dark-fraction that survives as د9's escape tag rather than being averaged away. (f) Extend readFingerprint to the six items criterion 12 enumerates, per-bubble uncertain set and glare and escape tags included, or the determinism gate is measuring the wrong thing. (g) Add criterion 14's ceilings as a third CI gate printed beside accuracy, and re-derive T_LO and T_HI against it, because putting the entire eraser-ghost range 0.2 to 0.5 inside the band blocks a paper for every erased answer and will not survive a 2 percent warning ceiling.
verdicts.verdict: The geometry half is the best reproducibility argument in the set and should be adopted essentially unchanged: the millimetre lattice, the continuity ban on thresholded operators, timing-mark row registration with a residual gate an order of magnitude under the row pitch, and the margin distribution as a leading-indicator CI gate. The photometry half is not buildable as written. It makes every bubble on the page hostage to two or three others, it carries no absolute floor and no saturation channel, it drops د7's per-row black even though it already holds the timing marks, it discards د9's escape signal into a percentile, and its own fingerprint does not compare what criterion 12 says to compare. As specified it produces confident blanks under glare and 49 ambiguous questions on a clean paper, so 99.7 percent with a 2 percent warning ceiling is not credible and the same paper twice is not guaranteed the same complete result. The design is honest about which constants are unmeasured, which is why the repair is cheap: six additions inside stages 8 to 10 and constants.ts, all of them named in FAILURE-MODES, none of them requiring a different engine.

verdicts.designName: Paper-Space Sampling: core-omr without a warp and without OpenCV
verdicts.lens: Buildability and testability starting today with no phone and no real photographs, plus maintainability: can the golden set be bootstrapped from our own renderer, is every file under 300 lines, can one person hold the code, and which tests would pass on a broken engine
verdicts.strongest: `readFingerprint` as a single canonical serialisation of the whole read (templateId, every question verdict, every field verdict) shared by two consumers that would otherwise each invent their own notion of agreement: the camera layer's rule-3 three-frame loop and the CI determinism gate. This is the one piece that makes acceptance criteria 8 and 12 mechanically checkable rather than aspirational, and criterion 12 in FAILURE-MODES 4ب-9 says exactly this ("تُقارَن النتيجة كاملة" including the uncertain-bubble set, not the score). Second and nearly as good: `geometry/group-meta.ts`, which joins back to `spec.questions[n-1].select` and `headerFields[i].usage` by position and never by id string. I verified the need: `decode.ts:70` synthesises `id: f${index}` so `f:studentId:2` becomes `f:f1:2` on the self-describing path while `usage` survives, and `BubbleGroup` carries neither `select` nor `usage`. Without that file, rule 2's `select:'many'` exception is unreachable and the id grid is unfindable on a device that never saw the template. Graft both regardless of which design wins.
verdicts.fatalFlaw:
Tier 0, the only test tier that can exist before the 300 photographs, is calibrated blind in precisely the place the confidence model lives, and no CI gate can see it. Two compounding halves.

First: the synthetic renderer draws no printed text inside bubbles. The design says "render a layout to a GrayImage" and never mentions glyphs; the prototype already on disk states it outright (`packages/core-omr/tools/render.ts:6-9`: "What it deliberately does not draw is text: no letter inside a bubble"). But `DEFAULT_THEME.bubbleLabel` is `#8c9196` at `bubbleLabelMm: 1.9` and `symbolsInBubbles` is true whenever `placement === 'internal'`, which STATUS.md section 4 confirms is the default. The design's own derivation of T_LO=0.30 rests entirely on that glyph ("a 1.9 mm glyph in a 2.48 mm core covers about 10% of the core area, contributing about 0.043 to ink"). So the single number that separates blank from uncertain is derived from an object the harness never renders. Worse, `theme.ts` DARKNESS_LEVELS change only `bubbleStroke`, `bubbleLabel`, `choiceLabel`, `frameStrokeMm`, `boxStrokeMm`, and the design's 0.62r core (1.24 mm) excludes the outline by construction (inner stroke edge at 1.84 mm). With no glyph drawn, the "3 print darknesses" axis of the advertised 8x6x4x3x5 sweep changes literally nothing inside the measured core. One third of the sweep's dimensions is decorative and reports as coverage.

Second: the three CI gates are accuracy, determinism, margin. Acceptance criterion 14 is absent. FAILURE-MODES 4ب-9 mandates a rejection ceiling of 2% of papers and a warning ceiling of 2% of questions on the ordinary tier, accuracy and rejection printed together always, and a build failure if any single environment stratum drops under 98% even when the aggregate passes. The design's testStrategy names none of that, has no ordinary/adversarial tier split, and measures no rejection or warned-question rate anywhere. This matters more for this design than for a rejection-shy one: stage 6 rejects on residual over 0.35 mm, on `too_oblique`, on `low_contrast` past 2% unmeasurable, on `unknown_template`; stage 11 voids an entire question if any one of its bubbles lands in the 0.30 to 0.55 band. Nothing in CI counts the cost. The design also does not cite criteria 11, 13 or 16 by number.

Together these mean the day-one harness reports green margins and clean determinism on a sheet population whose blank bubbles sit at ink 0 while the real ones sit at 0.03 to 0.08, and the first metric that would have caught the gap is the one gate the design left out.

Note also what the lens asked literally: FAILURE-MODES 4ب-10 item 6 prescribes synthetic marks composited over sheets produced by `sheet-pdf`, "وهي موجودة اليوم في `docs/samples/`". Ten such sheets do exist (I listed them, .pdf/.svg/.typ each). This design bootstraps from a third renderer it writes itself off `layoutSheet`, and never mentions `sheet-pdf` or `docs/samples/` at all. That is not fatal on its own, and there is a real reason (rasterising Typst output needs a dependency), but it is a divergence from ground truth that the design does not acknowledge or argue.
verdicts.concreteFailure: `standard50` on A4, printed at DARKNESS_LEVELS 'dark' where `bubbleLabel` is `#6a7176` (grey about 112 against paper 248 and fiducial black about 20), answered in 2H pencil under the auto-exposure compression FAILURE-MODES 4ب-7 warns about, giving a page range M-B of about 0.14. Glyph ink per covered pixel is (248-112)/228 = 0.60. Across the printed symbol set the glyph covers roughly 6% of the 0.62r core for a narrow symbol ('1', 'T', 'أ') and roughly 14% for a wide one ('8', 'W', 'ج'), so blank ink spans about 0.036 to 0.083 within one sheet at one darkness. That is a spread of 0.047, more than double the design's stated plus or minus 0.02. B = p30 lands near 0.045. A wide-glyph blank then scores (0.083 - 0.045) / 0.14 = 0.27, margin 0.03 below T_LO=0.30 and below the design's own p01 margin floor of 0.06; at M-B = 0.12 the same bubble scores 0.317 and is uncertain, and stage 11 makes its whole question ambiguous. With 250 bubbles and about 200 blanks on a 50-question sheet, a few percent of blanks crossing puts 8 to 16 of 50 questions in ambiguous, that is 16% to 32% warned questions against criterion 14's 2% ceiling and against د17's 5% blocked-papers target. Note the trap in the design's own constants: SHEET_UNMARKED_RANGE = 0.12 means a sheet at M-B = 0.13 is declared marked and then flagged nearly wholesale, rather than reported as unmarked. Now the testability half. Tier 0 renders no glyph, so every blank in the sweep sits at ink about 0, B about 0, and blank margins about 0.30, five times the gate. The 2880-cell sweep contains zero samples anywhere near this regime because the axis that would produce them (print darkness) has no effect inside the core when there is no glyph to darken. The accuracy gate does not run (no photographs). The determinism gate passes: three renders of one flat image through three homographies carry bit-identical graphite in paper space, so an engine that flags every question ambiguous flags them identically three times and scores a perfect determinism pass. The margin gate passes with 5x headroom. The build is green on the day the first real classroom stack turns into a review queue.
verdicts.salvage:
Four changes, all cheap now.

1. Render the glyph. Add a generated coverage table (same "generated data files" exemption CODING-STANDARDS section 1 already grants, and the same trick the design uses for `lattice.gen.ts` and `gf256.gen.ts`): for each symbol in the four preset alphabets, the fraction of a 0.62r core its 1.9 mm glyph covers, plus a coarse mask. Render it at all three `themeFor(darkness).bubbleLabel` values. This costs one generated file and makes the darkness axis of the sweep mean something. Without it, T_LO, T_HI and GROUP_GAP_MIN are untested numbers wearing a derivation.

2. Add criterion 14 to CI as a first-class gate, today, on Tier 0. Split the sweep into ordinary and adversarial cells; report reject rate, warned-question rate and accuracy together in one table, per cell, never aggregated alone; fail the build when an ordinary cell exceeds 2% warned questions or 2% rejected papers, and when any cell's accuracy falls under 98%. This is the gate that would have caught the failure above on day one, and it is the only gate that punishes the design for its own rejection-happiness.

3. Close the loop to the real printed artifact. Add one test that asserts the synthetic renderer and `sheet-pdf` agree: same layout, same geometry-bearing elements (fiducial rects, timing rects, code module origin and pitch, bubble centres and radii) at the same millimetres. Today they happen to agree on the code quiet zone (`sheet-pdf/src/render.ts:39-42` computes `moduleMm = box.wMm / (size + 2*quiet)`, `tools/render.ts:82` computes `box.wMm / (size + 8)`), but nothing enforces it and they are two files maintained apart. Also state plainly in the design that Tier 0 validates engine against layout and never layout against print, so nobody reads a green sweep as a claim about paper.

4. Re-budget the files against the evidence in this repo. The untracked prototype already implements the design's `code/` five-file block as `src/code/` (473 lines) plus `src/qr/` (843 lines), 1316 against the design's estimate of 780, and `src/geometry/fiducials.ts` is 209 lines for less than the design puts in its 190-line `detect/fiducials.ts`. `detect/timing.ts` at 190 lines is budgeted for five responsibilities (window search, 180-degree disambiguation, hypothesis scoring, pose refit, piecewise-linear row correction) against a "one responsibility per file" rule and will land past 300. Give per-file budgets to the QR five and pre-split `timing.ts` and `fiducials.ts` rather than discovering the 300-line cap at review time.
verdicts.verdict: The most buildable-today design of the four premises, and the only lens-relevant answer to "what do we write while the paper is being collected": a single `GrayImage` input, no CV library, no dual implementation, a first milestone that is genuinely a day's work and genuinely falsifies its own central claim if the three fingerprints differ. Its determinism argument is the best-argued reasoning in the document and its refusal of a pluggable CV port ("two implementations of a thresholding operator give two answers") is correct and should survive into whatever gets built. But under this lens it earns a 7, not more, because the tier it will live on for the next six weeks agrees with the engine by construction on geometry and is silent by construction on photometry, and because the one acceptance criterion written specifically to stop a rejection-happy engine from buying a green build (criterion 14) appears nowhere in its CI. The design is honest that Tier 0 is "a regression harness and never an accuracy claim"; it is not honest that Tier 0 is also not a calibration harness, which is the use it is actually put to when T_LO, T_HI, GROUP_GAP_MIN and SHEET_UNMARKED_RANGE each get "exactly one retune against the golden set". Build it, with the glyph table and the criterion-14 gate landing before the first threshold is tuned, not after.

verdicts.designName: Paper-Space Sampling: core-omr without a warp and without OpenCV
verdicts.lens: Portability and performance: one source on Hermes/React Native and Node/CI, inside the 400 ms of acceptance criterion 2. Typed arrays on Hermes, no WASM, YUV planes / row stride / rotation, memory churn per frame, pixels touched per paper.
verdicts.strongest: Millimetre-space lattice sampling taken directly off a stride-aware `GrayImage { width, height, stride, data: Uint8Array }`, with the 1000x1414 warp deleted. This is the one part I measured as unambiguously correct for both targets. All 540 bubbles of `full100` (verified count: `bubbleGroups` returns 104 groups / 540 bubbles) at 76 core + 40 ring samples is 63k bilinear samples, which I measured at 26 ms on Hermes and 8 ms on Node, a 3.3x engine penalty, exactly the range the design assumed. It is float arithmetic inside one function, which is Hermes's strongest path. The `stride` field is the right shape for both an NV12 Y plane (iOS) and YUV_420_888 plane 0 (Android, where Y pixel stride is guaranteed 1) with zero colour conversion, and it is trivially producible from a PNG in `test/`. And the two-anchor model has a portability property nobody else will get right by accident: because `ink = (white - core) / (white - black)` is a ratio of differences drawn from the same frame, it is invariant to the iOS `420v` video-range (Y in 16..235) versus `420f` full-range (0..255) split and to auto-exposure gain. Graft this whole half.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The Hermes penalty is not 3x to 8x. On the detection stage, which dominates, I measured it at 17x to 26x, and the design's CI gate is calibrated to hide exactly that. I implemented stage 1+2 verbatim (dec = max(1, floor(min(w,h)/384)), Int32Array integral over the decimated view, 7 scales h in {3,4,5,6,8,10,13}, box score at every position) and ran the identical script under `hermes-engine-cli` 0.12 and under Node 22 on the same x86 core: 1440p, 29 ms on V8, 495 ms on Hermes (17x). 1080p, 34 ms vs 633 ms (18.6x). 12 MP, 12 ms vs 284 ms (26x). Detection is dominated by typed-array indexed loads, which is the Hermes interpreter's weakest path, while measurement is float math, which is its strongest; the design took the 3-8x figure from the shape of the cheap half and applied it to the expensive half. Three compounding consequences. (1) Stage 2 alone at the 1440p frame that FAILURE-MODES 4ب-7 mandates is 495 ms on a desktop-class Hermes, already past the entire 400 ms of criterion 2, before refinement, homography, timing search, ink, or QR, and before PLAN rule 3's three agreeing frames, which makes the real per-scan budget about 130 ms. A Snapdragon-6-class core is roughly 3x slower again. (2) The design's own gate, "measured Node time x 8 must stay under 250 ms", passes: 29 x 8 = 232 ms. The gate certifies green a pipeline that is 10x over on the phone, and PLAN section 13 schedules the phone for weeks 7-8, three weeks after the 99.7% gate is meant to be locked. (3) The advertised cheapness is arithmetic the design states and never performs: it sells "63,000 bilinear samples instead of 1.4 million warp pixels" while its own stage 2 text says "1.3M box evaluations, each 16 integral reads", which is 20.8M reads, 15x the warp it deleted. My run measured 2.61M evaluations at 1440p, so 21M to 42M reads. FAILURE-MODES د13 budgets about 226,000 pixel reads for the entire agreement machinery inside the same 400 ms; this design spends roughly 100x that on one stage of one frame.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Two, both measured or checkable today. FIRST, the budget. A mid-range Android at the mandated 1440p: dec = floor(1440/384) = 3, view 853x480, 2.61M box evaluations. Measured 495 ms on Hermes on a fast x86 core, so roughly 1.4 s on a phone core, for fiducial detection alone; criterion 2 allows 400 ms for the whole result and rule 3 requires three scans inside it. Worse, `dec` is quantized by a short-side threshold, not a pixel budget, so the inversion is backwards: 1080p gives dec=2 and a 960x540 view (518k px) while 12 MP gives dec=7 and 576x432 (249k px). The cheaper phone does 2.1x the detection work of the flagship, measured at 633 ms versus 284 ms on Hermes. There is no headroom in `dec` either, because the scale list already starts at h=3. SECOND, and this is the one where CI is green and Android is dead: VisionCamera delivers the buffer in sensor orientation and exposes rotation as metadata (`frame.orientation`), it does not rotate the plane. A portrait-held Android phone hands core-omr a 90-degree-rotated raster. Stage 5 recovers the fiducial-rectangle aspect and compares against the hypothesis, so an A4 sheet arrives as 277x190 instead of 190x277, aspect 0.686 against an expected 1.458, "outside every hypothesis by more than 8%", and every scan returns `unknown_template`. Stage 5 carries only "both 180-degree labellings"; the correct labelling is not among the two tested. CI never sees this because fixtures are upright PNGs. And the repair is not free, because carrying four orientations quadruples the hypothesis work in stages 5 and 6, the second most expensive part of the pipeline. Add two smaller holes in the same family: `Uint8Array` cannot represent `420YpCbCr10BiPlanarVideoRange` (10-bit Y) which iPhone 12+ can deliver on some formats, and nothing anywhere in `packageLayout` owns buffer lifetime, so the 1.64 MB Int32Array integral is allocated per frame inside the loop PLAN rule 4 says must be strict about memory, on top of the 3.7 MB (1440p) to 18 MB (12 MP) full-buffer copy VisionCamera requires to get a plane into JS at all, which contradicts the design's phrase "with zero conversion".
verdicts.salvage: Five changes, and the first is the only structural one. (1) Stop searching the whole frame at seven scales. The fiducial's apparent size is not unknown, it is set by page fill, which the aiming UI already constrains, and the four squares are by definition near the four corners of the frame. Search four corner regions of roughly 15 percent of the frame at one or two scales, coarse-to-fine, which is a 15x to 25x cut and brings detection into the same order as the measurement half that already fits. (2) Make `dec` target a fixed pixel budget (about 150k px) rather than `floor(min(w,h)/384)`, which kills the inversion where 1080p costs 2.1x what 12 MP costs. (3) Delete the "x8" constant. `hermes-engine-cli` is an npm package that runs headless on Linux; I just used it. Run `tools/bench.ts` under the actual Hermes binary in CI on every PR. That single change, which costs an afternoon, is what would have caught this before a line of the engine was written, and it also removes a hidden tax the Node bench structurally cannot see: I measured that putting `box()` behind a module boundary, which the 300-line file cap and the one-responsibility-per-file rule push you toward, costs Hermes 474 ms versus 351 ms inlined (+35%) while V8 shows nothing, so the coding standards themselves are a device-only cost that a Node gate reports as free. (4) Budget the envelope, not the scan: criterion 2's 400 ms must contain rule 3's three frames or د13's perturbation set, so per-scan is about 130 ms and the design has to say so. (5) Retire the native escape hatch as written. Its contract is "bit-identical output against core-omr as the reference", but the only way a native kernel recovers 20x is NEON reductions and FMA contraction, and both change the summation order and rounding of the binary64 accumulations this design deliberately places upstream of its single threshold (luma-weighted centroid, bilinear ink, the normal-equations solve, p30/p99). Compile with `-ffp-contract=off` and unvectorized reductions to keep bit-identity and you give back most of the 20x. Ship it anyway as "close enough" and CI measures one program while the teacher runs another, which is precisely the two-implementations failure the design rejected option (b) for, restored through the back door, with a bubble at score 0.5501 in TypeScript landing at 0.5499 in NEON. Either state the native contract as "same decisions under a proven margin bound" or forbid the native path and design to the interpreter from line one.
verdicts.verdict: Half of this design is the best answer to the portability question I expect to see, and the other half was never costed. The CV decision is right and it is right for the reasons given: pure TypeScript over a stride-aware luma plane genuinely does run from one source on Hermes and in Node, it needs no WASM, it makes CI test the same code the teacher runs, and deleting the warp in favour of millimetre-space lattice sampling is both more deterministic and, measured, actually cheap (26 ms on Hermes for all 540 bubbles). Everything downstream of the pose is affordable. But the design replaced four OpenCV operations with a brute-force multi-scale box search over the entire frame and then advertised the result as cheaper than the warp while its own text states a read count 15x larger than the warp's. Measured on a real Hermes, that stage alone is 495 ms at the mandated 1440p on a desktop core, against a 400 ms budget that must also hold three frames, and the CI gate it proposes (Node x 8) passes at 232 ms and would let the whole team believe it fits until week 7. The rotation gap is a second, independent, ship-stopping defect that only Android reveals. Neither is unfixable and neither touches the parts of the design I would keep, but "no CV library" is only a defensible answer if the replacement for `findContours` is cheaper than `findContours`, and here it is not, and nobody checked. Send it back for a corner-constrained detector and a Hermes-run bench, then it is the strongest candidate.

verdicts.designName: Paper-Space Sampling: core-omr without a warp and without OpenCV
verdicts.lens: Coverage of docs/FAILURE-MODES.md: the scanner-resident defenses د7 to د16 and د20, and acceptance criteria 10 to 19
verdicts.strongest: Millimetre-space lattice sampling through H, combined with the per-bubble two-anchor physical ink scale (local paper white from the ring lobes, printed black from the fiducial interiors, ink expressed in [0,1] between them). This one keystone carries three defenses at once and carries them naturally. د11 stops being a special case: there is no warped raster and no x0.25 buffer, so "measure off the full resolution frame" is the only thing the code can express, and the second proven defect becomes unwriteable rather than merely fixed. د12 is natural because predicted timing marks are just more mm points to inverse-map, and the residual is already in millimetres, which is the unit د12's 0.5 mm gate is written in. And د13's deterministic perturbation set becomes nearly free: perturbing H and re-sampling roughly 63,000 lattice points is cheap enough to run per scan, where a warp-first pipeline must re-warp 1.4 million pixels for every one of the perturbations, which is exactly why د13's runtime substitute for frame agreement is usually written off as too expensive. Graft this even if nothing else survives. Note also that the per-bubble local white this design computes is precisely the quantity د10 requires ("pixels at 0.95 of the locally expected white") and that no warp-first design gets for free. The design builds the instrument for the defense it then omits.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: د10 is absent, and not merely unwritten: the pipeline's chosen operators destroy the evidence it needs before any stage could look. The words glare, specular and saturation appear nowhere in the thirteen stages, nowhere in the twelve tuned constants (CORE_R, RING_R, LOBE_DEG, WHITE_PCTL, BLANK_PCTL, MARK_PCTL, T_LO, T_HI, GROUP_GAP_MIN, TIMING_RESIDUAL_MAX_MM, MIN_PX_PER_MM, SHEET_UNMARKED_RANGE), and nowhere in the six enumerated rejections (no_sheet, unknown_template, geometry_unstable, too_oblique, low_contrast, layout_overflow). Three things then conspire. The core statistic is the MEAN over a 76-point lattice, and a mean is the one statistic that cannot separate "half specular white, half graphite" from "uniformly light pencil", although the 76 samples needed to tell them apart are already in hand. ink is then clamp01((white - core)/(white - black)), so a core brighter than its own local paper, which is physically impossible for graphite under diffuse light and is therefore the signature of specularity, is clamped to 0 and emerges as a maximally confident BLANK. And the only photometric guard, white - black < 28 levels, tests the denominator, so a glared bubble sails through it with maximum contrast. FAILURE-MODES puts specular graphite first among the three complaints that precede all others, attested by three independent vendors, and criterion 10 fails the build on a single wrong answer on a glare paper. This design's answer to that layer is not a rejection and not an uncertain bubble, it is a confident blank with a wide margin, which passes the design's own margin gate, its perturbation gate and the three-frame rule. Worse, the design's headline claim ("exactly one discretisation in the entire pipeline") actively fights the fix, because د10's rule is a count of saturated pixels over 10 percent of the disc area, which is a second thresholded operator upstream of the decision. The author would have to either break the central marketing claim or invent a continuous saturation measure, and nothing in the text shows awareness that the choice exists.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Second, independent, and arithmetically airtight on the design's own constants: the proven open defect returns one level up, because the design replaced per-question max(fill) normalisation with per-PAGE p99 normalisation, and p99 on real templates is a near-maximum order statistic. Measured in this repo: quick20 carries 120 bubbles so nearest-rank p99 is the 2nd darkest, standard50 carries 294 so it is the 3rd darkest, full100 carries 540 so it is the 6th. Take a standard50 sheet handed in with three answers erased and nothing else marked (PLAN section 4 names "مسح ممحاة" as a golden-set condition, and this design's own confidence section states an erased mark retains 20 to 50 percent of a full mark). Ink values: three ghosts at 0.20, the other 291 bubbles in the blank cluster which the design itself computes at B plus or minus 0.07. So B = p30 = 0.03 and M = p99 = 3rd darkest = 0.20. M - B = 0.17, which clears SHEET_UNMARKED_RANGE = 0.12, so the one guard does not fire. Each ghost then scores (0.20 - 0.03)/0.17 = 1.00, which is above T_HI = 0.55 with margin 0.45, and its runner-up scores 0.00 so groupGap = 1.00, far above GROUP_GAP_MIN = 0.30. Result: three CONFIDENT ANSWERS on a sheet the student answered zero questions on, at the widest possible margin, reproducible across every frame and every perturbation, and therefore invisible to criteria 8, 12 and 13. This is STATUS.md section 7's "أخطرها" defect, unchanged in mechanism, and it directly fails criterion 11, which requires a speck at 3, 5 and 10 times the noise floor to return '?' and NEVER a letter. The same missing floor fails criterion 11 in the other direction too: a sheet with two genuine light marks among 48 blanks gives M - B below 0.12, fires sheetUnmarked, and reports the two real answers as blanks. The design claims this defect is fixed by construction; it is fixed only for the literal 4 percent dust case on a page that also carries real marks, and it is re-created for the blank or nearly blank page, which is the more common and more damaging one. د8 forbids exactly this and specifies the remedy: an absolute minInkRatio of about 0.25 measured on the black-to-white scale of د7, which is precisely the scale this design already computes.
verdicts.salvage: Six changes, five of them small because the design already computes the inputs. (1) An absolute floor on ink before any page normalisation, per د8: no group may be resolved unless its darkest bubble clears minInkRatio on the fiducial-to-paper scale the design already produces, and p99 may serve as the mark anchor only when at least k bubbles clear that floor. One comparison, and it removes the fatal case above. (2) A glare channel taken from the 76 core samples already collected: count or, to preserve the continuity doctrine, softly integrate the excess above 0.95 times the same local white the design already computes per bubble; over the area fraction د10 names, the bubble becomes unmeasurable and goes to uncertain, never to blank, and the FRAME is rejected with a quadrant so the instruction can say which way to move. Emit that count with its own margin so it stays gated rather than a hard step. (3) An escape channel from the ring lobes, which are currently consumed only as a p70 white estimator, so that ink that left the bubble is flagged rather than discarded, per د9. This requires `placement` in geometry/group-meta.ts alongside `select` and `usage`, because د9 mandates masking the lobe on the label side when placement is 'external', and the design's group-meta recovers only two of the three. (4) A bilevel and histogram gate at the GrayImage boundary, per د16: a two-level scan currently enters this pipeline and reports maximum confidence on every bubble, which the document calls the worst possible failure for a product that promised not to guess, and the existing low_contrast test is the opposite test. (5) Split the rejection enum so causes match defects for criterion 16's 90 percent audit: code_unreadable with a "move closer" instruction and the د11 floor of 3 px per module (MIN_PX_PER_MM = 3.2 currently admits 1.6 px per module, which is below what any decoder resolves), separated from template_mismatch, separated from wrong_scale. (6) Read the timing marks photometrically as well as geometrically, per د7: they are solid black at every darkness level, one per row, already located, and they give the per-row black reference that a bilinear field over four corners cannot give when a hard shadow cuts the middle of the page. Also widen readFingerprint to carry the uncertain set and the glare and escape tags, since criterion 12 compares those, not just the verdicts. Two further notes for whoever builds this: the timing search window of plus or minus 2 mm reaches into the branding band, which layout/index.ts line 37 places at x = 12 mm with zero clearance from marks spanning x = 6 to 12 mm (د3 flags this and moves the strip), so the weighted centroid will be pulled by printed vertical text and can blow the 0.35 mm gate on good sheets, costing criterion 14's 2 percent rejection ceiling; and د1 changes the margins to 10 mm top and sides with 18 mm at the bottom, which invalidates the hardcoded "every fiducial centre sits 10 mm in from both nearest edges" shortcut and every number in the stage 5 aspect table.
verdicts.verdict: This design carries the geometric half of FAILURE-MODES better than the document asks and the photometric half thinly, and the split is not accidental: every defense it carries naturally is one that lives in the pose, and every defense it misses is one that lives in the light. Carried naturally: د11 (the reason the design exists; the x0.25 defect becomes unwriteable), د12 (best-carried defense in the design, with predicted-position matching, per-row piecewise-linear correction, residual gate and rotation resolved by evidence rather than assumption), د13's decision margin (emitted per bubble and gated in CI, and the architecture makes the perturbation set nearly free), د14's four states verbatim, د16's geometry gate (and better than asked, since it catches the sheet-spec paper-index encoding bug by verifying rebuilt geometry against marks on the paper rather than trusting the decoded spec), criterion 15 (scale invariance and the byte-identical grade across print percentages follow from mm-space sampling), and criterion 13. Carried awkwardly: د7 (per-bubble local white is excellent and finer-grained than the document asks, but black is bilinear over four corners only, and the per-row black reference د7 specifies is sitting unread in timing marks the design already locates, so a hard shadow cutting mid-page mis-scales the denominator by roughly 20 percent in the shadowed region), د8 (blank as a third state is carried well, the binarisation ban is carried by construction, the absolute floor is missing), د15 (structurally correct as a closed union with a never check, materially thin, and folding "code unreadable, move closer" into unknown_template is precisely the generic message د11 and د15 forbid), د20 (four of five marks symbols derivable, eraser trace not, because nothing detects it), criterion 12 (the fingerprint carries verdicts but not the uncertain set or the flags the criterion names). Structurally cannot, as written: د10 in full, د9's escape ring (the annulus is consumed for the opposite purpose and `placement` is unavailable in group-meta), د16's image gates (a bilevel scan enters and reports maximum confidence), criterion 10 (fails on one wrong answer, and this design produces confident blanks under glare), criterion 11 (fails in both directions on the arithmetic above), criterion 16's cause-matching audit. There is also a ratchet the author should see: because glare produces confident wrong answers rather than rejections, this design will look GOOD on criterion 14's rejection ceiling while failing criterion 10, which is the exact trade FAILURE-MODES built criterion 14 to make visible. Score 6 through this lens alone: the geometric skeleton is the best of what I have seen and should be built, but two of the nine or so scanner defenses are absent by construction and one of them is complaint number one in the field research, so this is not yet a design that can be built as written. None of the six salvage items is large, and the design already computes the inputs for four of them, which is the fairest thing that can be said about it.

verdicts.designName: Millimetre-native scanner: no warp, no OpenCV, no photograph needed to prove it
verdicts.lens: Accuracy and reproducibility on real classroom photographs: is 99.7 percent credible, and is the same paper photographed twice guaranteed to yield the same COMPLETE reading including which bubbles were flagged uncertain (criterion 12)?
verdicts.strongest: The two-point photometric chain in `score/photometry.ts`, and specifically the third point nobody else has: black K from the four fiducial interiors corrected per row by that row's own timing mark, white W from each bubble's own 1.15r to 1.55r annulus at the 70th percentile, and then subtraction of the printed glyph baseline. This is د7 executed better than د7 asks for. The repository proves the glyph matters and no other input names it: `sheet-pdf/src/theme.ts` prints `bubbleLabel` at `#8c9196` (normal), `#b0b5ba` (light) and `#6a7176` (dark), at `bubbleLabelMm: 1.9` inside a 4 mm bubble, so an empty bubble carries roughly 0.04 to 0.08 of apparent fill that varies by a factor of two with a print setting the scanner cannot see. Any absolute ink floor (د8, the fix to the open proven defect) is meaningless until that offset is removed, and this is the only design that removes it from the sheet in hand rather than from a constant. The 70th percentile on the annulus rather than the mean is also right: it survives the external-label ink that `externalLabelMm: 3.2` puts at 2.8 to 4.4 mm from the bubble centre, which overlaps the annulus. Graft the K-per-row / W-per-bubble / baseline-removal structure whole. Replace only how the baseline number is obtained.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The per-symbol baseline is a rank statistic over a population whose composition the student chooses, and it has a hard cliff. `thresholds.ts` sets `BASELINE_PERCENTILE 0.25`, and stage 13 states the assumption out loud: "since fewer than 75% of bubbles are ever filled, that percentile is the empty baseline". That is true of bubbles in aggregate. It is false per symbol, which is the axis the estimator actually keys on. The moment more than 75 percent of the bubbles carrying one symbol are shaded, the 25th percentile lands inside the FILLED cluster, b_s jumps from about 0.08 to about 0.65, and f = (d - b_s)/(1 - b_s) clamps every one of that symbol's marks to exactly 0. The guard `BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES 8` counts samples, not fill rate, so it never fires. Every downstream defence then reports success on the wrong answer: max f is 0, so the group is `blank` and not `uncertain`; the absolute floor F_BLANK 0.30 confirms the blank; there is no doubleMarked and no uncertain bubble, so `counts` is `{doubleMarked:0, blank:N, uncertainBubbles:0}`, the clean-scan signature; and because the defect is a deterministic function of the sheet rather than of the pose, all three shots agree, `readingDigest` matches, `agree()` accepts, and acceptance criteria 8 and 12 both PASS on a wrong grade. This is the STATUS.md section 7 defect, "a confident answer on a question the student did not answer", reintroduced with its sign reversed: a confident blank on a question the student did answer. It reaches production through paths the repository already supports, not exotic ones: `trueFalseSymbols()` ships in `alphabet.ts`, `ChoiceQuestionSchema` accepts `symbols` of length 2, and `select: 'many'` is rule 2's intentional exception that this design advertises as a headline feature. Secondary, and each independently disqualifying against the 23 defences: (1) no glare channel at all. د10 is the single most-cited field cause of misreads across three independent vendors and criterion 10 drops the build on ONE silent error under glare, yet the design's only response is the risk-section claim that "photometry calibrates against printed targets ... so a global glare or ink shift cancels", which is a category error, because specular glare is a local saturated lobe, is pose-dependent by construction, and is precisely what a disc MEAN cannot separate from unshaded paper. No pixel is ever counted against local white, no frame is ever refused for saturation. (2) Criterion 12 is literally uncompletable here: it compares "الإجابات، والفراغات، والغامض، وغير المؤكد، **ووسوم الوهج والهروب**، وحالة المعرّف", and this design emits neither a glare tag nor an escape tag. The 1.15r to 1.55r annulus IS د9's escape ring, but it is consumed as a white reference and its 70th percentile deliberately DISCARDS the ink that د9 exists to detect. (3) No decision margin per bubble (د13), so criterion 13's deterministic perturbation sweep has nothing to key on. The design's answer is a wide band, but a band has two edges, and the marked/uncertain edge at f = 0.35 flips exactly as readily as the edge it replaced. (4) The determinism argument budgets sigma for n only, never for f, yet the absolute gates on f (0.35, 0.30, 0.20) are the load-bearing fix. (5) `MIN_PX_PER_MM 3.0` is half of د11's floor, which at `codeModuleMm: 0.5` demands 6 px/mm and a page spanning 1260 px; the design admits frames from which its own self-describing path cannot read the code. (6) Its central determinism claim, "sample lattices are keyed by millimetres, not pixels", is contradicted by its own `disc.ts` and stage 12, both of which set the step to `min(0.25 mm, 1.2 px)`, a pixel-dependent quadrature rule. (7) Timing marks sit at x in [6,12] mm, so a per-row y correction from a single left-edge mark cannot see or correct the x displacement that a curled page produces at mid-page, and stage 11 absorbs residual rather than gating on it, which is the opposite of د12.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Executed the design's own rule (`BASELINE_PERCENTILE 0.25`, f = clamp((d - b_s)/(1 - b_s))) with d = 0.08 for an empty bubble carrying the printed 1.9 mm glyph (the design's own stated 0.06 to 0.10) and d = 0.65 for an HB pencil mark after two-point calibration. A 50-question true/false sheet, one symbol pair, `BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES 8` satisfied at 50 samples per symbol. Student answers T on 37 of 50: fill rate 74 percent, b_T = 0.080, f(marked) = 0.620, every T reads FILLED, score correct. The SAME sheet with the student answering T on 38 of 50: fill rate 76 percent, b_T = 0.650, f(marked) = 0.000 and f(empty) = 0.000, so max f = 0 for all 38 of those groups, every one reports `blank`, `uncertainBubbles` is 0, `doubleMarked` is 0, and the paper scores 12 out of 50 instead of roughly 45. One extra True flips 38 questions from correct to silently blank. The cliff is at exactly 75 percent and one question wide. Two further inputs cross it with no true/false sheet involved: a `select: 'many'` question set where symbol A is shaded on 17 of 20 questions (85 percent) gives b_A = 0.650 and every A reads blank, which lands squarely on rule 2's intentional exception; and a 12-column student id grid where the id contains 10 zeros (83 percent for symbol '0') gives b_0 = 0.650, so every zero column reads empty and `StudentIdReading` returns `partial` or `unset` for an id that is fully and legibly shaded, which then fails د14's reconciliation and produces the duplicate record criterion 9 promises to prevent. Zero-heavy student ids are exactly the case د22 calls out. In every one of these the result is bit-identical across all three shots, so the design's `agree()`, its P2 pose-invariance property, criterion 8 and criterion 12 all report green. Separately, on glare: a shaded bubble at W = 205, K = 32, graphite grey 95 gives d = 0.636 and f = 0.61, comfortably FILLED. Reshoot the same paper at a different angle so a specular lobe covers 35 percent of the inner disc at 250: the disc mean becomes 149, d = 0.322, f = 0.263, which is below F_SURE 0.35 and puts max f into [0.20, 0.30), so the group flips from "answered B" to `uncertain`. Nothing in the design detects that 35 percent of the disc was saturated rather than blank. Two photographs, two different complete readings, criterion 12 broken, `agree()` never converges, and the teacher sees the "it will not scan" state that FAILURE-MODES names as the highest-volume support topic in the whole category.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, all additive, none touching the architecture. (1) Cap the baseline by physics, not by rank. The printed glyph is drawn by us and bounded by `theme.ts`: at worst `#6a7176` over a 1.9 mm glyph inside a 2.8 mm disc it cannot exceed about 0.10. Set b_s = min(percentile(d_s, 0.25), BASELINE_CEIL) with BASELINE_CEIL 0.15, and refuse the frame (not the group) when the raw percentile exceeds the ceiling, because that condition means the estimator's assumption is violated and the design should say so rather than compute through it. Additionally require the symbol's d distribution to be bimodal with the lower mode holding at least 25 percent of the mass, and fall back to b = 0 with a widened band otherwise. Add a property test that sweeps fill rate from 0 to 100 percent per symbol in one-question steps and asserts monotonic f, which is the test that would have caught this and which the current P3 (monotonicity in planted coverage, at fixed fill rate) structurally cannot. (2) Add the saturation channel د10 requires as a THIRD number out of `sample/disc.ts`, alongside disc mean and annulus percentile: the fraction of disc lattice points above 0.95 W_i. Above about 10 percent the bubble is unmeasurable and must route to `uncertain`, never to `empty`, and the frame is refused with the quadrant of the saturation named so the instruction can be directional. The pipeline already visits every lattice point, so the cost is one comparison per sample. (3) Emit a decision margin per bubble (د13) as the distance from f and from n to the nearest threshold each would have crossed, put both the glare tag and an escape tag (ink in the annulus, computed from the samples already taken, masked on the label side when `spec.questions[n-1].placement === 'external'`) into `readingDigest`, and refuse any paper carrying a margin under a measured floor. This is what makes criterion 12 evaluable at all and what turns criterion 13's perturbation sweep from an assertion into a measurement. (4) Raise `MIN_PX_PER_MM` from 3.0 to 6.0 to match د11, and either fix the lattice step to a pure millimetre quantity or drop the claim that the estimator is distance-invariant, because `min(0.25 mm, 1.2 px)` changes the number of samples from about 178 to about 44 across the admitted resolution range and the design's determinism section rests on the opposite.
verdicts.verdict: The skeleton is the best of what I can see: millimetre-native forward sampling with no warp, timing-mark scoring used to VERIFY paper, template and rotation rather than assume them (which converts the A5-decodes-as-A4 encoding bug into a named refusal), a decision-projection digest that excludes fill ratios, and a photometric chain calibrated from targets the sheet itself prints. All of that should survive into whatever gets built. But through this lens the design is not yet buildable, and the reason is not that it is missing polish. FAILURE-MODES did not exist when it was written and it shows: of the defences that live in the scanner, it carries د7, د8, د11 partially and د12 partially, and it carries none of د9, د10, د13 or د16. The single most-cited real-world cause of wrong reads has no channel in it, and its one sentence on the subject argues that glare cancels, which is the exact inversion of why glare is dangerous. Meanwhile the estimator it invented to make the absolute floor honest, which is genuinely the best idea in the submission, contains a data-dependent cliff at 75 percent per-symbol fill that produces a confident blank on a fully answered question, reproducibly, across every shot, on a `select: 'many'` sheet or a zero-heavy student id. That is a silent wrong grade that passes criterion 8, criterion 12, the three-frame agreement rule and the entire five-tier test strategy, because every one of those tests compares the engine against itself. 99.7 percent is not credible under this design as written, and repeat-shot determinism is guaranteed only for the readings that are already unambiguous. It IS credible under this design with the four salvage items, and the salvage is a week of work, not a rewrite. Score 5: half a good engine, with the half that is missing being precisely the half that a teacher holding a wrong grade would have needed.

verdicts.designName: Millimetre-native scanner: no warp, no OpenCV, no photograph needed to prove it
verdicts.lens: Buildability and testability starting today with no phone and no real photographs, plus maintainability
verdicts.strongest: The three-rung bootstrap plus the self-arming corpus harness. `test/corpus/<sheetId>/{meta.json, shot-01..03}` written now, a structural test asserting every directory holds at least three shots (which makes acceptance criterion 8 impossible to under-fill by construction rather than by discipline), a determinism test over the shots of one sheet, and `if (sheets.length >= 30) expect(accuracy).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.997)` so the gate switches itself on the day the thirtieth paper lands with no PR to enable it. Above it, the rung ladder answers the lens question concretely and cheaply: print twenty sheets and flatbed-scan at 200 dpi this week (real toner, real paper, real print-scale error, no perspective), then photograph flat on a desk, then handheld, all entering the same harness so a regression names which rung it came from. That is the only proposal here that produces non-synthetic pixels within days without a phone, and it should be grafted verbatim. Graft alongside it the source scan that walks `src/` and fails on `Math.sin|cos|atan2|exp|log|pow|hypot|**`, which turns a determinism promise into a lint rule that cannot be lost in a refactor.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The design deletes the QR decode stage and outsources it to "a QR *string* from the platform barcode API", so the self-describing path has no implementation and no CI test on either target, and the line budget that justifies "one person can hold it" silently excludes it. This is not a gap the design names honestly; it is load-bearing three times over. (1) It destroys the design's own headline argument. Rejected-A was refused because "the golden set would certify the Node path while the phone runs the other" and because it "drags a native module into a package the plan requires to know nothing about the camera" - which is precisely what a platform barcode API is. There is no barcode API in Node, so every CI accuracy number is measured on a path where the spec was handed in by the test, while the teacher's device takes a path with a native decoder in it that CI never executes. One implementation on both targets was the whole point and this breaks it at the one stage that matters most. (2) Defence د11 is unimplementable from outside. د11 requires the code be measured off the full-resolution frame at a specific ROI with a floor of 3 px per module and a named "move closer" refusal; ML Kit and iOS Vision take a whole frame and return a string or nothing, so the design cannot enforce its own floor, cannot emit that refusal from the closed enumeration د15 requires, and cannot distinguish "no code found" from "code too small". The brief lists this as one of two proven defects that must be correct from the first line; the design moves it out of the package instead of fixing it. (3) It makes stage 10's advertised catch of the A5 encoding bug unreachable. Stage 10 scores a candidate against "a decoded code payload" and the claimed win is that a wrong declared paper becomes a refusal - but nothing in this design ever produces a decoded payload, and criterion 15 / د16's geometry gate compares the measured aspect against "the paper declared in the code" with nothing declaring it. Cost of the omission, measured in this repo: the working tree's in-progress `src/qr/` is 891 lines across eight files (gf256, reed-solomon, versions, format, blocks, payload, layout, index). That is 45 percent again on top of this design's ~2000-line `src` estimate, appearing nowhere in the 16-file table. Every "one person can hold it" and "everything after the first milestone is addition rather than restructuring" claim is computed against a budget missing its largest single component.
verdicts.concreteFailure: Two, and the second is what makes the first invisible until a teacher is holding the paper. (a) Which tests pass on a broken engine: replace all of `score/photometry.ts` with `d_i = 1 - m_i/255` - no annulus W, no fiducial or timing-mark K, no two-point calibration at all, the file the design says "makes the relative rule work under shadow, because both references are local" - and `loop.test.ts` plus P1, P3, P4, P5, P6 and P8 all stay green. On `tools/synth` output the paper is near-255 and the ink near-0 by construction, so two-point calibration is arithmetically a no-op; the multiplicative illumination field in degrade.ts is smooth and global, which the 0.20-wide normalised band absorbs; and P2 asserts on the decision *digest*, which is invariant to any monotone photometry. So tiers 0 through 3 certify a scanner with no photometric calibration. Tier 3 cannot rescue it: it compares coordinates only, and its stated mechanism is wrong about the artifact - `docs/samples/*.svg` contains zero `<rect>` and zero `<circle>` elements (706 `<path class="typst-shape">`, bubbles as four cubic Bézier arcs in a local frame at `M 0 0 M 0 5.6692915 C ...`, positioned by an ancestor `<g transform="translate(...)">`), so "parse out the drawn rect and circle coordinates" is a nested transform-stack walk plus a Bézier centre fit, and even done perfectly it never touches a pixel value. The nightly poppler rasterisation that would have compared pixels is conditional on poppler, which is not installed, and `typst-ts-node-compiler` exposes only pdf/svg/plainSvg/html/vector/query with no raster method - so nothing in the design ever compares its forward model's *photometry* to the real artifact. Meanwhile `theme.ts` shows `bubbleLabelMm: 1.9` is a font size, not an ink area, and the design renders that glyph as "a stroked stand-in with calibrated ink area" - one author-chosen number standing in for per-symbol coverage that varies by more than 2x between an Arabic `ه`, a Latin `W` and a digit `1`. b_s, BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES 8, F_BLANK 0.30 and F_SURE 0.35 are all calibrated against that stand-in and are unfalsifiable until the thirtieth real photograph. (b) The field consequence the suite cannot generate: a filled bubble under specular reflection off graphite, which FAILURE-MODES 4ب-1 ranks the number one cause of misreads at two independent vendors. The disc saturates, so mean disc intensity m_i = 255 while the annulus 70th percentile W_i stays at paper level, say 205, with K_row = 30. The design's own formula gives d_i = clamp((205 - 255)/(205 - 30), 0, 1) = clamp(-0.286, 0, 1) = 0.000, then f_i = clamp((0 - b_s)/(1 - b_s), 0, 1) = 0.000, quantised to 0/1024. The one bubble carrying the answer reports exactly the same number as a bubble no pencil ever touched. The other three sit at baseline, so max f over the group is under 0.30 and the question is reported `blank` with `uncertainBubbles: 0` - a silent wrong grade, in the state د8 defines as "the student's decision". `degrade.ts`'s listed effects are illumination field, shadow half-plane, blur, noise, ink darkness, paper grey and eraser ghosts: no saturation model, so no seed in the 5,000-case sweep can produce this. `photometry.ts` has no saturated-pixel count, so د10's "over roughly 10 percent of the disc it is not light, it is unmeasurable" has nowhere to be computed. `decide.ts` has three bubble states, so `unmeasurable` has no representation and cannot be surfaced. Criterion 10 drops the build for one such answer, and the design's risk register names glare, then defers it to "when a real photograph fails, add its failure mode to degrade.ts" - deferring to real photographs the single defence its whole angle claims real photographs are not needed for, when a bright saturated blob is the cheapest thing in the entire degradation list to synthesise.
verdicts.salvage: Four changes, all before the first milestone, because three of them are restructuring rather than addition. (1) Put the QR image decoder back inside `src` and inside the budget: binarise the full-resolution crop at the box `layout.code.box` gives you, locate the three finder patterns, sample the module grid, then format-info, de-interleave, GF(256) Reed-Solomon, payload. Budget it at the ~900 lines and eight files the repo's own working tree already demonstrates, hold each under 200, and enforce د11's 3 px per module floor as a named member of the closed rejection enumeration. If instead the self-describing path is genuinely out of MVP scope, say so in writing, make stage 10 read the spec only from a device-local catalog, and delete the claim that stage 10 turns the A5 encoding bug into a refusal - that claim is currently unreachable and it is doing persuasive work it has not earned. (2) Add a fourth bubble state `unmeasurable` and a frame-level glare refusal to `types.ts` *before* `decide.ts` is written, count pixels above 0.95 of locally expected white inside the disc, and replace `clamp(d, 0, 1)` with a tagged result so that d below 0 (saturation) and d at the ceiling stop being spelled the same way as a legitimate reading. Add specular blobs and a directed point source to `degrade.ts` in the same PR, and add the P-case: a planted answer under a synthetic glare spot must return uncertain or refuse, never blank. This touches types, thresholds, photometry, decide, scan, read/sheet and agree - seven of sixteen files - which is why it cannot wait. (3) Make Tier 3 compare pixels, not coordinates. A rasteriser as a test-only devDependency is permitted by exactly the argument the design already uses for its JPEG decoder, and it converts the single independent check from a coordinate diff into an assertion that the forward model's ink, glyph coverage and stroke rendering match the artifact a printer will actually emit. Without it the constants in `thresholds.ts` are self-certifying. While there, rewrite the Tier 3 description to match the artifact: nested transform stacks and Bézier centre fits, not rects and circles. (4) Widen `readingDigest` to criterion 12's full projection - answers string, blank set, ambiguous set, per-bubble uncertain set, glare and escape tags, id state. As written the digest covers per-question status only, so `agree()` accepts three frames that disagree about which bubbles were flagged, which is the exact non-determinism criterion 12 exists to catch, in the one function the design offers as camera-free proof of rule 3. Add د13's requirement that agreement counts only between measurably different poses (corner movement at least 2 percent of page width or 3 degrees), since three identical frames from a propped phone prove nothing and the design's `agree()` currently accepts them.
verdicts.verdict: The best-argued geometry in the set, resting on a test ladder that stops exactly where the sheet stops describing itself. What is right is very right: deleting the 1000x1414 warp is correct and the reasoning for it (1.414 fits only the A family, and resampling injects pose-dependent error into the number determinism depends on) is the strongest single insight offered; the mm-native lattice, the absolute floor with a separate `blank` state, the positional correlation of `headerFields` to `gridFields` because only `usage` survives the printed code, P7 iterating PAPER_NAMES against a bug that fails today, and the banned-transcendentals source scan are all load-bearing and all correct. File sizes are credible - nothing over 190 estimated lines, well inside the 300 cap - though the sibling implementation in this working tree suggests the estimates run roughly 2x light where the logic concentrates (photometry 230 actual against 110 estimated, pipeline 240 against 155). But through this lens the design fails its own thesis twice. It claims every stage is provable in CI from images we generate today, then hands the code-reading stage to a platform API that CI cannot call and omits ~900 lines from its budget for it; and it builds an entire five-tier suite whose synthetic tiers stay green with the photometry file replaced by a one-line stub, while the only independent check it proposes compares coordinates and never pixels - and is described in terms of SVG elements the artifact does not contain. The result is a design that can be started this week and will produce a green CI, an accuracy number about our model of a sheet, and a first real photograph that finds the whole scoring path uncalibrated. Fixable, not discardable: the geometry stack, the corpus harness, the rung ladder and the transcendental ban should all survive into the synthesis. The QR decoder, the saturation state and a pixel-level cross-check against the real artifact have to be in the budget before the first line, not after the first photograph.

verdicts.designName: Millimetre-native scanner: no warp, no OpenCV, no photograph needed to prove it
verdicts.lens: Portability and performance: one source on Hermes/React Native and Node/CI, inside acceptance criterion 2's 400 ms, given typed arrays without a JIT, no WASM, YUV planes with stride and rotation, per-frame memory churn, and pixels touched per paper
verdicts.strongest: Deleting the 1000x1414 warp and sampling every bubble forward through H in millimetre space, on the full-resolution frame. This is the one decision that is right on every axis at once and it is now measured, not argued: an implementation of exactly this architecture already sits uncommitted in /home/user/transferchecker/packages/core-omr/src (scan/pipeline.ts, measure/bubble.ts, geometry/frame.ts) and I ran it. A whole standard50 sheet (55 groups, 294 bubbles) at 1440x2560 costs 25 ms in V8 with the perturbation set off, and the cost is nearly flat from 3.7 MP to 12.2 MP (25/31/37 ms) because only fiducial search scales with frame size while bubble sampling scales with the sheet. The warp it replaces is 1.41 M bilinear fetches on every frame regardless. It also removes a pose-dependent interpolation from the exact number determinism rests on, and it dissolves contradiction 7.3 (1000x1414 fits only the A family) for free. The banned-transcendentals scan over src/ is the second thing worth grafting: an engine-portability rule enforced by a test, which almost nobody writes. Note the on-disk code already violates it (measure/bubble.ts:68 uses Math.hypot to build the sample lattice, so two engines that round hypot differently would include different lattice points and produce different fill ratios), which is precisely the class of bug that test exists to catch.
verdicts.fatalFlaw: The design has no model of the pixel format it consumes, and that is what makes the two targets diverge silently. Its central promise is "one implementation, one set of numbers, on both targets", and it defends the CV decision with the line that the camera's Y plane is "already grayscale, so the plan's grayscale step costs nothing". That equivalence is false. The forward model in tools/synth/render.ts composites coverage into 8-bit code values (the on-disk raster.ts:31 does exactly this: before*(1-alpha) + value*alpha), which is LINEAR light. A camera's Y plane is the gamma-encoded, often video-range luma of BT.601/709, and degrade.ts's "multiplicative illumination field" is likewise a linear-light operation applied to code values. Every absolute constant in thresholds.ts (F_BLANK 0.30, F_DEAD 0.20, F_SURE 0.35, ADAPT_C 12, MIN_CONTRAST 40) is therefore calibrated in a colour space no phone ever produces.
